spelling(node, database, release=None, via=None)

Return how database spells an external identifier at a release, on one link or over all.

The name of an external node is its canonical spelling: the one Ensembl gives at the latest release in which the identifier exists. Where databases, the releases of one database, or the genes a database attaches it to write an identifier with different letter case, the graph keeps one node and remembers how each link (the identifier, an Ensembl id, a database) wrote it at each release: Tc (a synonym of one mouse gene) and tc (a synonym of Noto) are one node whose links say which gene carries which spelling.

A release counts as the assembly that serves it in the backbone has it (serving_assembly): an earlier assembly that Ensembl keeps beside the primary one (human GRCh37, frozen with the spellings of its time) does not supply the spelling of a release that the primary assembly serves.

Parameters:

  • node (str) – An external node.

  • database (str) – The database whose spelling is wanted.

  • release (int | None) – The release at which the database is read. None: the latest release at which the database has the identifier (on the link, with via).

  • via (str | None) – The Ensembl id at the other end of the link (a gene, transcript or translation). None: the spelling that most links of the database give at the release, then the one with more upper-case letters, then the first in sort order.

Returns:

The spelling at that release; at a release at which the link (or the database) does not have the identifier, its spelling at its latest release; the node name where nothing differs from it.

Return type:

str

Raises:

UnknownIdentifierError – If the node, or via, is not in the graph.

symbol_case()

Return how the organism’s symbol databases write their symbols, read from the graph (decisions 55 and 80).

"mixed" when more than half of the names that the organism’s symbol databases (idtrack.organisms.SYMBOL_DATABASES) attach to genes, at any release, are written with a small letter (MGI writes Trp53: 98 % of mouse symbols), else "capitals" (HGNC and VGNC write TP53: 3 % of pig symbols have a small letter, as C1orf112 has). In an organism that writes its symbols in mixed case, a string in one letter case is read first as a symbol without letter case (readings()).

to_directed(as_view=False)

Returns a directed representation of the graph.

Returns:

G – A directed graph with the same name, same nodes, and with each edge (u, v, k, data) replaced by two directed edges (u, v, k, data) and (v, u, k, data).

Return type:

MultiDiGraph

Notes

This returns a “deepcopy” of the edge, node, and graph attributes which attempts to completely copy all of the data and references.

This is in contrast to the similar D=MultiDiGraph(G) which returns a shallow copy of the data.

See the Python copy module for more information on shallow and deep copies, https://docs.python.org/3/library/copy.html.

Warning: If you have subclassed MultiGraph to use dict-like objects in the data structure, those changes do not transfer to the MultiDiGraph created by this method.

Examples

>>> G = nx.MultiGraph()
>>> G.add_edge(0, 1)
0
>>> G.add_edge(0, 1)
1
>>> H = G.to_directed()
>>> list(H.edges)
[(0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 1), (1, 0, 0), (1, 0, 1)]

If already directed, return a (deep) copy

>>> G = nx.MultiDiGraph()
>>> G.add_edge(0, 1)
0
>>> H = G.to_directed()
>>> list(H.edges)
[(0, 1, 0)]

to_undirected_class()

Returns the class to use for empty undirected copies.

If you subclass the base classes, use this to designate what directed class to use for to_directed() copies.

Graph files: their names, the identity a file records, and finding the files of a folder.

A graph file’s name tells graphs apart that can sit in one folder: graph_<organism>_assembly<primary assembly>_min<first>_max<last>[_sessions][_forms<a-b>][_extall].npz. What a name does not say (the selection of external databases, the organism table, the format version) is in the record inside the file (idtrack.graph.GraphRecord; idtrack.graph.TheGraph.load() checks it). Nothing here needs the network, a table or PyYAML: the selection of external databases is given as parsed content.

What one gene is: the one rule of the package for telling whether gene ids name the same gene.

Ensembl gives a gene a new stable id more often than the gene changes: a model is replaced by one at the same place, two models are merged, a gene is annotated again on an alternative locus, an assembly patch or an LRG record beside the reference sequence. Several stable ids can therefore stand for one gene, and a rule that counts genes by stable id counts these as several. The rules that ask how many genes an identifier names over the releases (decision 73: an entry of idtrack.build.database_manager.ONE_GENE_ONLY links genes only where it names one gene; decision 74: a label of more genes than an identity can is a family name, idtrack.TheGraph.label_families), the rule of bridges (decision 72: an id is evidence of a lineage only where it leaves one gene for another at the same place) and the Y copies of pseudoautosomal genes (decisions 93 and 95, idtrack.TheGraph.y_copies()) read it here, from what the graph holds of Ensembl’s own tables (the count of genes at one release, idtrack.TheGraph.genes_linked_at_once(), counts stable ids; it says why):

  • places (idtrack.TheGraph.places(), from Ensembl’s gene and seq_region tables): two genes are at one place when, on one assembly, a place of one shares a base with a place of the other on one sequence region and one strand (overlap()). Places are compared base by base on the reference sequence; a patch, a haplotype, an alternative locus or an LRG record lies on a sequence of its own, whose coordinates are not those of the reference sequence;

  • places carried across an assembly change (idtrack.TheGraph.carried_places(), decision 103): where Ensembl publishes a mapping of an earlier assembly onto a later one (its chain files, idtrack.build.assembly_chain), a place on the earlier assembly is carried onto the later one by its aligned bases at build, and compared there by overlap as places on one assembly are; where Ensembl publishes none (pig Sscrofa10.2 to Sscrofa11.1, the macaques), places of two assemblies are compared by the names of their sequences only (below);

  • the region a patch or a haplotype stands for (idtrack.TheGraph.assembly_exceptions(), Ensembl’s assembly_exception table of each release): a gene on a patch or a haplotype is a copy of, or an alternative to, a gene of that region of the reference sequence, so it and a gene whose places share no base with the region (on either strand) lie apart; inside the region the bases are not compared (the table maps the region, not each base);

  • what a sequence is (idtrack.graph.types.Place.kind, from Ensembl’s coord_system and seq_region_attrib tables): a chromosome (CHROMOSOME), the mitochondrial genome (MITOCHONDRIAL) or a sequence below them (SCAFFOLD: a scaffold, a supercontig, a contig). The assemblies of one organism name its chromosomes alike from one to the next (by its karyotype), and an organism has one mitochondrial genome; so across assemblies, where no base can be compared, two genes whose places all lie on such whole sequences, and on no sequence of the same name (the mitochondrial genome compared by its kind), lie apart. A scaffold’s name says nothing of where its bases lie in another assembly;

  • outside the reference sequence (idtrack.TheGraph.non_reference_releases(), Ensembl’s non_ref attribute of a sequence region): a gene that never lies on the reference sequence is a copy of, or an alternative to, a gene of the reference sequence, never a gene of its own;

  • Ensembl’s history (the stable-id events between two stable ids): an id that Ensembl’s history carried to another id that follows it (no release at which both live) is that gene under another id. Two ids that live at one release are two genes unless their places overlap at that release, whatever history they share: a split of one id into two ids that then live side by side is Ensembl saying “two genes”;

  • a region that repeats another: a pseudoautosomal region of Y is the same sequence as the region of X it repeats, so a place in it is read on that region of X (idtrack.organisms.pseudoautosomal_repeats(), GRC’s regions, equal to Ensembl’s PAR assembly exceptions): the Y copy of a pseudoautosomal gene, which Ensembl gives an id of its own from release 110, lies at its gene’s place (decisions 93 and 95).

The rule of bridges compares two genes by their places only (relation(), the keys of idtrack.results.PLACE_RELATIONS: the walk follows Ensembl’s history itself), over every version of each stable id; the explained path compares the two versions of a history step the same way (idtrack.results.PathStep.places). The count of genes (count_genes()) counts what the graph shows apart on one assembly and by the names of whole sequences, and no more: ids that nothing tells apart (holders on two assemblies without a history link and without a comparable place) are not counted as two genes; it does not read the places carried across an assembly change or the regions of the copies, which only relation() compares.

Copies are not grouped with their own gene of the reference sequence: Ensembl’s alt_allele table says which gene of the reference sequence a copy is an allele of, but the graph does not read it (Ensembl’s core databases fill it for human, for mouse at some releases and not at 115, and not for pig or the macaques at 115); a copy therefore adds no gene to any count.

a region of Ensembl’s coordinate system chromosome, or a region Ensembl ranks in the organism’s karyotype (attribute karyotype_rank: the chromosomes of an assembly that Ensembl loads with one level of sequences, primary_assembly).

Type:

Carried

(assembly, region, start, end, strand) (GeneFacts.carried).

Type:

alias of Iterable[tuple[int, str, int, int, int]]

class GeneFacts(reference, outside, placed, spans=(), alive=0, outside_at=0, sequences=None, carried=mappingproxy({}), regions=mappingproxy({}), region_sequences=None)[source]

Where a gene lies and when it lives, as far as idtrack.graph.genes compares genes.

The fields: reference, its places on the reference sequence by assembly ({assembly: (segment, ...)}, every version together); outside, whether it lies outside the reference sequence at some release; placed, whether the graph holds any place of it (a graph made in memory holds none); spans, every place on the reference sequence with the releases at which it is there ((assembly, segment, release mask)); alive, the releases at which it lives (a bit mask; 0 when the graph does not say); outside_at, the releases at which it lies outside the reference sequence; sequences, the names of the sequences of its places on the reference sequence when every one of them is a whole sequence (WHOLE_SEQUENCES; the mitochondrial genome named by its kind), else None; carried, its places on the reference sequence carried onto later assemblies by Ensembl’s mapping of the assemblies ({assembly: (segment, ...)}); regions, the regions of the reference sequence that its places outside it stand for (Ensembl’s assembly exceptions), on their own assembly and carried onto later ones ({assembly: ((region, first base, last base), ...)}, on both strands); region_sequences, the names of the sequences of those regions on their own assembly when every one is a whole sequence, else None.

count_genes(stable_ids, facts, joined, release=None)[source]

Return how many genes some stable ids name: the size of a set of them that the graph tells pairwise apart.

A copy (GeneFacts.copy: it lies only outside the reference sequence) adds no gene: it stands for a gene of the reference sequence; copies alone stand for one gene. The other ids are compared in each frame in which the graph can tell loci apart:

  • one release: the ids that live at it and lie on the reference sequence there; ids whose places at that release overlap (one region, one strand; a chain of overlaps among the ids counted) are one locus, every other id is a locus of its own (two ids that live at once are two genes unless their places overlap, whatever history they share: a split of one id into two that then live side by side is two genes);

  • one assembly: the ids placed on its reference sequence, over its releases; ids whose places overlap are one locus, and so are ids of one lineage (Ensembl’s history carried one to the other where they follow one another, no release at which both live); a later id at another place without a history link is another locus;

  • the names of whole sequences across assemblies: the ids all of whose places lie on chromosomes or the mitochondrial genome; ids on a sequence of one name, or of one lineage, are one group (a gene of chromosome 15 in one assembly and a gene of chromosome 6 in the next are two).

Two ids are told apart when a frame that holds both puts them at two loci. The count is the size of a set of ids that are pairwise told apart, built from the frame that shows the most loci (one id of each of its loci, the first by id) and extended, in the order of the ids, by every other id told apart from each id of the set so far, the other ids of that frame among them (a gene of chromosome 1 of the next assembly beside five genes that live apart on other chromosomes at once is a sixth gene; two genes at one place at one release that lie apart at the next are two). The set is built in this order, not searched for the largest, so the count is a lower bound of the most ids told pairwise apart. Ids that nothing tells apart are one gene: holders on two assemblies without a history link and without a comparable place, or ids of which the graph holds neither a place nor the releases at which they live, are not evidence of two loci.

Parameters:

  • stable_ids (Collection[str]) – The stable gene ids (without version).

  • facts (Mapping[str, GeneFacts]) – {stable id: facts}; an id missing here has NO_FACTS.

  • joined (Mapping[str, Collection[str]]) – {stable id: stable ids} that Ensembl’s history carried it to or from; an id missing here has none.

  • release (int | None) – Count at this release only (the frame of one release; an id that does not live at it adds none).

Returns:

The number of genes; 0 for no id, at least 1 for some.

Return type:

int

joins_mitochondrial_and_nuclear(graph, older, old_release, newer, new_release)[source]

Tell whether a history step joins a gene of the mitochondrial genome and a gene of a nuclear sequence (decision 91).

One version lies on the mitochondrial genome at its side of the event, the other has a place at its side and none on the mitochondrial genome (a chromosome or a scaffold: the kind says it is nuclear, whatever the relation of the two places across an assembly change). A version without a place there is no evidence either way.

  • new_release (int) – The first release of the new side.

Returns:

bool

In this order: same_place when, on an assembly on whose reference sequence both lie, a place of one overlaps a place of the other (same_place()); places_apart when they lie on the reference sequence of a common assembly and no places overlap there; else, where a place of one was carried onto an assembly on whose reference sequence the other lies (Ensembl’s mapping of the assemblies, decision 103), same_place when a carried place overlaps a place of the other there and places_apart when none does; else, where either lies outside the reference sequence, places_apart when the reference region a copy stands for (Ensembl’s assembly exception) shares no base with what the other stands for, or lies on whole sequences of other names, and outside_reference otherwise; else no_place when the graph holds no place of either; else places_apart when they lie on whole sequences of different names (on_other_sequences(): two chromosomes, or a chromosome and the mitochondrial genome, which no assembly change turns one into the other); else other_assemblies.

class Track(graph, search=None)[source]

Bases: object

Convert a gene identifier of one Ensembl release into its counterpart at another release.

Track(graph) holds a graph (idtrack.graph.TheGraph) and answers from it. How a conversion works (convert()):

  1. Starting release. With from_release the identifier is read at that release and must be active there. Without it the identifier is read at the target release if it is active there, and at the latest release at which it is active otherwise. The rule is the same for every kind of identifier.

  2. Entry. An identifier that is not a versioned gene id is replaced by the genes it stands for at the starting release: a gene id without version by its version of that release, any other id by the genes that Ensembl’s cross-references of that release attach it to.

  3. History. From those genes the search follows Ensembl’s stable-id history (version changes, merges, splits, retirements) forward or backward in time until the target release. It is a best-first search over states (gene, release): every state is expanded once, so the work is bounded by the size of the part of the history that the query can reach, and every call has a budget. A step between a gene of the mitochondrial genome and a gene of a nuclear sequence is no lineage and is not followed (decision 91; the explained path lists it among the refused steps).

  4. Bridges. Only when the history leads to no gene at the target release, the search may pass from a gene to another gene that carried the same external id (or the same transcript) at the same time or later (the gap in releases is reported), at most idtrack.settings.SearchSettings.bridge_limit times, and it uses as few bridges as possible. A bridge is taken only where it is evidence that one gene became the other: never through a synonym; where the two genes lie on the reference sequence of one assembly, only when their places overlap there; from or to a copy outside the reference sequence, only through an id both carried at one release that names one gene at each such release; elsewhere (their places cannot be compared), only when no release gave the id to both (idtrack.results.BRIDGE_RULES). The explained path lists every bridge considered with the rule that took or refused it (idtrack.results.BridgeCheck).

  5. Copies beside the reference sequence. Genes on alternative loci and assembly patches, and LRG records, leave the answer when a gene of the reference sequence was reached too; they are reported apart.

  6. Final conversion. Each gene found is reported as itself or converted to the ids of final_database that are attached to it at the target release.

  7. Ranking. Every (gene, target) pair is ranked, best first, and the best answer is marked; it is several pairs when the identifier stands for several genes equally (a tie). idtrack.engine.ranking holds the rules.

Throughout, an edge of the graph counts at a release only on the assembly that serves that release (the primary line of releases): an earlier assembly that Ensembl keeps serving beside a newer one (GRCh37 beside GRCh38) is not part of a conversion.

Results never depend on the order of sets or on the hash seed of the process.

graph

The graph that is queried.

Type:

TheGraph

search

The default budget and bridge rules of a conversion (a call may give its own).

Type:

SearchSettings

Create the engine of a graph.

Parameters:

  • search (SearchSettings | None) – The default search settings; None for idtrack.settings.SearchSettings’s defaults.

Raises:

ArgumentTypeError – If search is not a idtrack.settings.SearchSettings.

convert(identifier, from_release=None, to_release=None, final_database=None, *, from_database=None, allow_bridges=True, return_ensembl_alternative=True, explain=False, search=None)[source]

Convert an identifier to the target release and, if asked, to a target database.

Starting release: with from_release the identifier is read at that release and must be active there. Without it, the identifier is read at to_release if it is active there (the answer is then what the identifier means at the target release), and at the latest release at which it is active otherwise. A gene id without version stands for its version of the starting release. The rule is the same for Ensembl ids and for ids of external databases.

Search: from the genes the identifier stands for, Ensembl’s stable-id history is followed to the target release. Only when that leads to no gene, and allow_bridges allows it, the search passes through an external id or transcript that two genes carried at the same time or one after the other, with as few such bridges as possible (idtrack.results.Candidate.bridges: 0 is history only). A bridge is taken only where it is evidence that one gene became the other (never through a synonym; on one assembly only between genes whose places overlap; from or to a copy outside the reference sequence only through an id both carried at one release that names one gene at each such release; elsewhere only through an id that no release gave to both: idtrack.results.BRIDGE_RULES).

Final conversion: with final_database the answer is first a gene: the genes found are ranked as Ensembl genes (below), and a target in the final database is an id of that database attached at the target release to a gene of that best answer. One result has one final database: the genes of the best answer that have such an id are returned with it (where only some of a tie have one, those); if none of them has one, the genes themselves are returned (no_target), or nothing with return_ensembl_alternative=False. Another gene the search reached is never answered by its id (it stays a candidate of the view all where it has one).

Copies beside the reference sequence: Ensembl also annotates genes on alternative loci (haplotypes) and assembly patches, and LRG records (LRG_<number>, fixed reference sequences of single genes), each with a stable id of its own and with the names and accessions of the gene it is a copy of. Which genes these are is Ensembl’s statement, kept in the graph (idtrack.graph.TheGraph.is_non_reference() at the target release); nothing is read off an id. When the search reaches genes of the reference sequence and such copies, the copies are not candidates; they are listed in alternative_locus_genes. When it reaches copies only (the identifier is such a gene or an LRG record, or a name that only they carry), they are the answer.

Identity: a gene id that exists at the target release is its own answer. The queried gene id’s own version at the target release is never taken out as a copy (a gene that lay on a patch of the assembly of the target release is still that gene), it comes first, and it is the best answer whatever else its history reaches.

Ranking (idtrack.engine.ranking): every (gene, target) pair is ranked by the confidence of the final conversion, the number of bridges, the release gap of the bridges, the query being the entry gene’s display name at the starting release (Ensembl’s own name of the gene there: idtrack.graph.TheGraph.display_releases()), the support of the query on the entry gene (the number of databases that attach the identifier to that gene at the starting release, to the gene itself or to one of its transcripts or translations), both the best over every entry gene from which the search reaches the gene (several where the history merges genes: decision 106), the path score, being the query itself, the number of cross-reference and history steps, and the ids. The best answer: the queried gene id’s own version at the target release when the search reached it; otherwise the entry genes with the best confidence, bridges, gap, display name and support each contribute their best successor (by score, then being the query itself, then, between successors of the one gene that are still equal, the richest annotation). If more than one gene or target remains, the answer is a tie. The candidates come best first, the pairs of one gene together.

Parameters:

  • identifier (str) – The identifier. The graph says which node the string means (idtrack.graph.TheGraph.resolve_name() for from_release, without one for the last release of the graph, and for from_database). A transcript or translation id without version stands for its version of the starting release.

  • from_release (SupportsIndex | None) – The Ensembl release the identifier comes from, an int or another integer type (numpy.int64). None: see above.

  • to_release (SupportsIndex | None) – The target Ensembl release. None: the last release of the graph.

  • final_database (str | None) – The database to convert the genes into. None or ensembl_gene: the genes themselves; base_ensembl_gene: gene ids without version; else an external database of the genome assembly of the target release.

  • from_database (str | None) – The external database the identifier is meant as (its ids, and where none of them matches, the synonyms it records): only the genes that this database attaches it to are entered, and an identifier that is not an id of that database (an Ensembl id, an id of other databases only) has no conversion. Between the genes entered, the one that more databases attach the identifier to is still the better supported. None: all databases.

  • allow_bridges (bool) – Allow bridges through external ids when the history leads to no gene.

  • return_ensembl_alternative (bool) – When no gene found has an id in final_database, return the genes themselves instead of nothing.

  • explain (bool) – Record the paths (Conversion.path, and the step indices of each candidate).

  • search (SearchSettings | None) – The budget and bridge rules of this call; None: search.

Returns:

The candidates, ranked, the best marked; without candidates, the reason.

Return type:

Conversion

Raises:

  • ArgumentTypeError – If identifier or a database is not a string, a release not an integer, a flag not a boolean, or search not a SearchSettings.

  • UnknownReleaseError – If a release is not one of the graph.

  • UnknownDatabaseError – If final_database is not available at the target release or from_database is not an external database of the graph.

  • InactiveAtReleaseError – If from_release is given and the identifier is not active at that release.

  • UnknownVersionError – If the identifier is an Ensembl id with a version that the graph does not hold and that cannot be newer than the graph, or an accession with a version that its links never attached and that cannot be newer than the graph (below the latest, or of an accession not attached at the last release).

  • SearchBudgetExceededError – If the search needs more states or time than the budget of the call.

This is the final conversion of convert() for one gene. The ranking of the candidates of a conversion.

The order of every (gene, target) pair, the best answer, and the criterion that decided between the best answer and the runner-up.

Pure functions of what the search found; nothing here reads the graph except through the annotation counts that the caller passes as a function.

A pair is ordered by its key (Pair): being the queried gene id’s own version at the target release; then how its entry gene compares with the other entry genes (the lineage: final confidence, bridges, gap of the bridges, the query being the entry gene’s display name at the starting release, support of the query on the entry gene; where the history merges several entry genes into the gene, the best display rank and support of them all, decision 106), then how its gene compares with the other successors of the same entry gene (within: steps without a score, mapping score, being the query itself), then steps and ids.

Of the evidence of which gene a name stands for at a release, Ensembl’s display name of a gene (gene.display_xref_id) is Ensembl’s own statement of the gene’s name there; support counts the databases that attach the name to a gene, of which a projection or a symbol that NCBI attached to another gene’s translation is one like any other. So among the genes that carry a name at one release the gene whose display name it is ranks first, and support decides between genes that are equal in it (two genes that both display the name, or neither). The display name holds for the string as it is typed (decision 102): letter case is evidence where the string has mixed case (Foxl1 is not the display name FOXL1 of another gene); a string in one letter case carries none, and in an organism whose symbols are written in mixed case the display name of a name authority, read without letter case, ranks before another source’s (mouse GAPDH is the gene that MGI displays as Gapdh before the gene that UniProt displays as GAPDH). A name authority’s symbol against another gene’s synonym is decided before both, when the string is read (decision 94: every name of a release before any synonym, idtrack.graph.TheGraph.resolve_name()).

The best answer: the pairs of the queried gene id’s own version when the search reached it, else all pairs; of those, the entry genes that are equal in the lineage evidence all belong to the answer. The mapping score compares the successors of one entry gene (it says how much of that gene a successor keeps, not which of two genes a name stands for), then being the query itself, and between successors that are still equal the richness of annotation decides, as the last resort. What remains is the answer; more than one pair is a tie, given in ascending order of gene id and target id.

LINEAGE_CRITERIA: tuple[str, ...] = ('final_confidence', 'bridges', 'bridge_gap', 'display_name', 'entry_support')

The criteria of the lineage, in the order of Pair.lineage (named as idtrack.results.CRITERIA names them).

The explained path of a conversion: the steps the search took, typed, and the nodes they pass, as data.

The search records each path as a tuple of raw steps: (source, target, key) for a history edge, (source, target, 0, release) for a cross-reference edge used at a release (None for the final hop of confidence 1), and (None, gene, None) for a gene that is its own answer. PathBuilder turns them into idtrack.results.PathStep and idtrack.results.PathNode records with what the graph says about each (releases, scores, splits and merges, databases and assemblies, where each gene lies and whether a history step moves it), every step and node once per conversion, and the bridges the search considered with the rule that took or refused each (idtrack.results.BridgeCheck).

class GraphChecks(graph, database_manager, *, details_limit=50, search=None)[source]

Bases: object

The self-tests of a graph: checks that compare a built graph with Ensembl’s tables and with itself.

GraphChecks(graph, database_manager) holds a graph, the manager of the tables it was built from, and an engine (idtrack.engine.Track) over the graph. It has two groups of methods, for developers and for the end of a graph build. Nothing here changes the graph.

Checks (is_...). Each states one invariant of a built graph and returns a CheckResult: whether the invariant holds, and what was compared and found. A check does not raise for what it finds: a violation is a result that does not hold, and so is anything that keeps the check from being completed (a table that cannot be read, a release without identifiers), with the error in the result’s details. So the checks can be run one after the other, and a result is never mistaken for success: its truth value is the verdict.

Conversion runs (history_...). They convert the identifiers of a database at a release and count what happened to them; they return the counts and raise an idtrack.errors.InputError for arguments that cannot be used, before anything is searched (a database that the graph does not hold, a release or assembly it does not have), naming the argument and what is valid.

Ensembl keeps one genome assembly per release as the primary one, and an earlier assembly can stay listed beside it (human GRCh37). A release therefore exists per assembly: the checks ask the manager for an assembly first and for the release second, and compare assembly by assembly.

Typical use:

checks = GraphChecks(api.graph, API.database_manager("homo_sapiens", 115, "./idtrack_cache"))
result = checks.is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl()
if not result:
    print(result.details)
graph

The graph.

Type:

TheGraph

The manager of the tables the graph was built from.

DatabaseManager

The engine over the graph, used by the conversion runs.

Track

history_travel_testing(from_release, from_assembly, from_database, to_release, final_database, allow_bridges, strategy, convert_using_release, from_fraction=1.0, progress=True, progress_details=False, return_ensembl_alternative=False)[source]

Run an end-to-end Ensembl-history conversion and collect granular QA metrics.

The routine samples identifiers from from_database/from_release (optionally down-sampling via from_fraction) and converts each one to final_database/to_release using idtrack.engine.Track.convert(). It is intentionally non-fatal: every failure mode is caught, logged and tallied so that large regression suites can run unattended. All results are returned in a single nested metrics dictionary whose structure mirrors the printable report that history_travel_testing_random() logs.

The statistics fall into four conceptual groups; each counter not only records an absolute event count but also serves as a red-flag indicator for specific classes of mapping pathology. Use the guidelines below to interpret the numbers and decide whether a run is healthy, questionable, or action-required.

  • Failure / anomaly counters

    • history_voyage_failed_gracefully - the converter declined with one of its two named errors: idtrack.InactiveAtReleaseError (the id is not active in the graph at the release it was taken from) or idtrack.SearchBudgetExceededError.

    • history_voyage_failed_unknown - any other unexpected exception.

    • lost_item - traversal finished but produced no final IDs.

    • lost_item_but_the_same_id_exists - special case of lost_item when the target and source DB are both Ensembl-gene and the target ID still exists in the graph.

    • found_ids_not_accurate - at least one returned target ID is not part of the authoritative ids_to reference set.

  • Mapping quality

    • one_to_one_ids - queries that resolved to exactly one target ID.

    • one_to_multiple_ids - queries with > 1 admissible targets.

    • one_to_multiple_final_conversion - subset of the above where exactly one traversal path was found (heuristics eliminated alternatives).

  • Collision analysis

    The list clashing_id_type == [clash_one_one, clash_multi_multi, clash_multi_one] classifies target IDs that were reached by more than one query:

    • clash_one_one - every colliding query was 1→1.

    • clash_multi_multi - every colliding query was 1→many.

    • clash_multi_one - mixture of 1→1 and 1→many queries (most alarming category).

  • Timings & book-keeping

    • time - wall-clock runtime in seconds.

    • conversion - per-query mapping result for all successful traversals.

    • converted_item_dict / converted_item_dict_reversed - raw per-ID caches used to derive the higher-level counters above.

    • parameters - echo of the function arguments.

    • ids - the sampled from and reference to ID sets.

Parameters:

  • from_release (int) – Ensembl release number of the source IDs.

  • from_assembly (int) – Genome assembly code of the source IDs.

  • from_database (str) – Node-type / database of the source IDs.

  • to_release (int) – Ensembl release number of the target IDs.

  • final_database (str) – Node-type / database to convert into.

  • allow_bridges (bool) – Permit temporary detours through external IDs when native Ensembl history edges break.

  • strategy (str) – Count the best answer of each conversion (best) or every candidate (all) (idtrack.results.STRATEGIES).

  • convert_using_release (bool) – Pass from_release straight into idtrack.engine.Track.convert() instead of letting it infer the starting point.

  • from_fraction (float) – Fraction (0 < x ≤ 1) of the ids_from population to sample; speeds up smoke tests.

  • progress (bool) – Show tqdm progress bar (coarse).

  • progress_details (bool) – Embed live metric counters in the tqdm postfix.

  • return_ensembl_alternative (bool) – Forwarded to idtrack.engine.Track.convert().

Raises:

  • UnknownDatabaseError – If a database is not one that the graph holds; nothing is converted then, and the message lists what is valid. A source is an external database of from_assembly or the Ensembl ids of a form of the graph, named by their node type (ensembl_gene, base_ensembl_gene) or by their label on the assembly (assembly_<key>_ensembl_<form>; the name of a form, gene, is not a database). A target is a database that idtrack.engine.Track.convert() takes as final_database at to_release (idtrack.engine.Track.final_databases()). Also if to_release is not a release of the graph, or from_fraction is outside the interval (0, 1].

  • ArgumentTypeError – If a database is not a string.

  • InvalidArgumentError – If strategy is not best or all.

Returns:

Nested metrics dictionary with the layout described above.

history_travel_testing_random() logs it as a human-readable summary.

Return type:

dict

Notes

  • All counters are absolute counts - divide by len(metrics['ids']['from']) to obtain rates.

  • The collision analysis is inspired by the clash statistics logic implemented at the end of the function and helps spot discrepant “unique” IDs that suddenly become ambiguous. Keeping all three clash counters at zero is the gold standard for a healthy build.

is_base_is_range_correct(progress=True)[source]

Check that a gene id without version exists exactly where one of its versions does.

For every gene id without version two ways of saying where it exists must agree:

  1. the releases of the edges from the id to its versions, on any assembly (idtrack.TheGraph.combined());

  2. the union of the releases of its versions on any assembly (idtrack.TheGraph.get_active_ranges_of_base_id_alternative(), which also refuses a version whose edges contradict its history; that is reported as a difference too).

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene ids), n_differing and differing (per gene id its id, the ranges of its edges and of its versions, or the contradiction of a version).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_combined_summary_complete()[source]

Check that every node has a summary of its cross-reference edges, except the two placeholders of an id.

idtrack.TheGraph.combined() sums what the cross-reference edges of a node say, by the kind of the node (the edges that enter a gene, the edges that leave any other node). Every node of a built graph has such edges, with two exceptions by construction: <id>.Void and <id>.Retired, the nodes that stand for “before the id existed” and “after it was retired”, which only the history touches.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_without_summary and without_summary (nodes that no cross-reference edge touches, or whose summary is empty), n_placeholders_with_summary and placeholders_with_summary.

Return type:

CheckResult

is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes()[source]

Check that only genes of the backbone are linked to nodes of their own type.

The graph has layers: the history links gene versions of the backbone with each other; every other edge links nodes of two different types (an external identifier and a gene, a transcript and its gene, a gene id without version and its versions). An edge between two nodes of one type that is not the backbone’s is a violation.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_same_type and same_type (pairs of linked nodes of one type that is not the backbone’s, with the type).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_final_external_conversion_robust(convert_using_release=False, final_database=None, to_release=None, progress=True, from_fraction=1.0, strategy='all')[source]

Check that every gene of a release converts to the ids that an external database gives it there.

The genes of a release are converted, at that release, into an external database that attaches its ids to genes, and each conversion is compared with the manager’s table of external identifiers of the assembly that serves the release. The invariant holds when every gene that the table gives an id converts to exactly those ids (letter case ignored), and no gene converts to an id that the table does not give it. A gene without an id in the database converts to nothing; that is the only loss that is not a violation. The entries the build left out by decision 73’s rule (idtrack.TheGraph.entries_of_several_genes) are no ids of the table here.

Parameters:

  • convert_using_release (bool) – Give the release to the conversion as from_release (otherwise the engine chooses where the gene id is read).

  • final_database (str | None) – The external database. None: drawn at random among the external databases that attach ids to genes (at to_release, when that is given).

  • to_release (int | None) – The Ensembl release. None: drawn at random among the releases at which the database has ids (of any such database, when final_database is None too).

  • progress (bool) – Show a progress bar and log what is tested.

  • from_fraction (float) – The fraction of the genes that is converted (0 < x <= 1).

  • strategy (str) – best: compare the engine’s best answer only; all: every candidate.

Returns:

details: database, assembly, release, compared (the number of genes converted), and four kinds of violation, each with its number (n_...) and first examples: different (converted to other ids than the table’s: id, converted, expected), unexpected (converted although the table gives the gene no id), lost_with_id (not converted although the table gives the gene an id) and failed (the conversion raised). Also lost (every gene that was not converted, with or without an id in the table) and run (the counts of history_travel_testing()). A check that could not be made (no database and release to draw, a release at which the database has no ids, a release the graph does not have) does not hold and says why in error.

Return type:

CheckResult

Raises:

  • UnknownDatabaseError – If final_database is not an external database of the graph that attaches its ids to genes; nothing is converted then, and the message lists what is valid.

  • ArgumentTypeError – If final_database is neither a string nor None.

  • InvalidArgumentError – If strategy is not best or all.

is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl(progress=True)[source]

Check that the gene ids of the graph are those of Ensembl’s id tables, on every assembly at every release.

For each genome assembly and each release that the assembly has in the graph, the gene ids with their versions are read from the id table of that assembly and release (through the manager) and from the graph (the genes that the graph has on that assembly at that release, idtrack.TheGraph.trios()). The two sets must be equal: no gene of the table is missing in the graph and the graph has no gene that the table lacks.

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of assembly-release pairs), n_differing and differing (per differing pair its assembly and release, the numbers n_missing and n_extra, and the first ids missing in the graph and extra in it).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_id_functions_consistent_ensembl_2(progress=True)[source]

Check that every gene version is referred to exactly at the releases of its history.

For every gene id with version of the backbone, two things the graph says independently must agree:

  1. The releases of its edges: the releases at which the gene is referred to (by its id without version, its transcripts, external identifiers) on the assembly that serves the release (idtrack.TheGraph.combined(), idtrack.TheGraph.serving_line). A gene that lived on an earlier assembly is referred to there at the releases that assembly served.

  2. The releases of its history: where Ensembl’s id history, validated against the id tables, has the version (idtrack.TheGraph.active_releases()).

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene versions), n_differing and differing (per gene its node and the release ranges edges and history).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_id_functions_consistent_external(progress=True)[source]

Check that the external identifiers of the graph are those of Ensembl’s tables.

For each genome assembly and each release that the assembly has in the graph, and for every external database, the identifiers of the manager’s table of external identifiers (of every form of the graph) are compared with the identifiers the graph has for that database, assembly and release (idtrack.TheGraph.trios()). Both differences count: an identifier of the tables that the graph lacks, and an identifier of the graph that the tables do not have (the kind of error that produces wrong mappings). The graph keeps one node for identifiers that differ in letter case only, so the comparison ignores letter case; an identifier of the tables that is itself an Ensembl id of the graph is no external identifier there (idtrack.TheGraph.misplaced_external_entries) and is left out, and so is an entry of idtrack.build.database_manager.ONE_GENE_ONLY that the build left out because the tables give it to several genes over the releases of the graph (idtrack.TheGraph.entries_of_several_genes).

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar per assembly.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of database-assembly-release triples), n_differing and differing (per differing triple its database, assembly and release, the numbers n_missing and n_extra, and the first identifiers missing in the graph and extra in it, in lower case).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_node_consistency_robust(progress=True)[source]

Check the two rules of the graph’s edges: no edge within a layer but the backbone’s, one edge between layers.

Beside the rule of is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes(), two nodes of different types are linked by exactly one edge: what the databases say about the pair at all releases is the content of that one edge (idtrack.graph.Connection). Several edges are allowed only between gene versions of the backbone (one per event of the history).

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of nodes), n_same_type and same_type as in is_edge_with_same_nts_only_at_backbone_nodes(), n_several_edges and several_edges (pairs of nodes of different types with more than one edge, with their types and the number of edges).

Return type:

CheckResult

is_range_functions_robust(progress=True)[source]

Check that no two versions of one gene id are active at the same release.

The versions of a gene id follow one another in Ensembl’s history: at every release of the backbone an id has one version at most. For every gene id without version the release ranges of its versions on the backbone (idtrack.TheGraph.active_ranges()) are compared pair by pair; any release that two of them share is a violation.

Parameters:

progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

details: compared (the number of gene ids), n_overlapping and overlapping (per pair the id, the two versions and the releases they share, as ranges).

Return type:

CheckResult

random_dataset_source_generator(assembly, include_external, include_ensembl, for_final_database, only_backbone_tests, release_lower_limit=None, form=None)[source]

Draw a database of a genome assembly and a release at which the graph has it.

The databases to draw from are chosen by the switches; of them only those that the graph has on the assembly at some release (at or after release_lower_limit, when that is given) can be drawn, and the release is one of theirs.

Parameters:

  • assembly (int) – The genome assembly.

  • include_external (bool) – External databases of the assembly can be drawn (synonyms excepted).

  • include_ensembl (bool) – Ensembl ids can be drawn: the gene ids of the backbone with and without version (ensembl_gene, base_ensembl_gene) and, unless for_final_database, the ids of the assembly (assembly_<key>_ensembl_<form>).

  • for_final_database (bool) – The draw is a target: the ids of one assembly are no target of a conversion.

  • only_backbone_tests (bool) – Draw ensembl_gene whatever the other switches say.

  • release_lower_limit (int | None) – The earliest release that can be drawn.

  • form (str | None) – Only databases that attach their ids to this form (gene, transcript, translation), and the Ensembl ids of this form.

Returns:

(database, assembly, release); None when none of the databases to draw from has a release that can be drawn.

Return type:

tuple[str, int, int] | None

Raises:

InvalidArgumentError – If the switches leave no database to draw from (neither external databases nor Ensembl ids, and not the backbone alone).

Harmonization

Harmonization: the features of several datasets converted to one Ensembl release and database.

The pure core (convert_features(), feature_table(), output_plan(), STATUSES) needs pandas only. HarmonizeFeatures, which reads and writes .h5ad files, needs the harmonize extra (pip install 'idtrack[harmonize]': anndata and scipy); without it, using the name raises an ImportError that says so; it is left out of __all__, so that from idtrack.harmonize import * works without the extra.

convert_features(api, feature_names, to_release, final_database, from_release=None, from_database=None, progress=False)[source]

Convert the feature names of one dataset, then name every gene reached in the final database.

The names of a gene in the final database depend on the gene, the database and the release only, so they are read from the gene itself (idtrack.API.gene_to_database(): a few look-ups per gene, no search), whatever feature led to the gene and whatever name that feature’s own conversion returned.

Parameters:

  • api (Any) – An idtrack.API with the graph.

  • feature_names (list[str]) – The feature names.

  • to_release (int) – The target release.

  • final_database (str) – The final database.

  • from_release (int | None) – The release the names come from; None: read each where the graph holds it.

  • from_database (str | None) – The external database the names are meant as; None: any.

  • progress (bool) – Show a progress bar.

Returns:

The results (one per feature, in order) and {gene: final-database names} (sorted; empty for a gene without an id in the final database).

Return type:

tuple

feature_table(feature_names, matchings, gene_names)[source]

Classify each input feature of one dataset by its conversion; a pure function of that dataset alone.

Parameters:

  • feature_names (list[str]) – The dataset’s feature names, in file order.

  • matchings (list[ConversionResult]) – idtrack.API.convert() results, one per feature, in the same order (their best view counts).

  • gene_names (dict[str, list[str]]) – {ensembl_gene: names}: the final-database names of every gene reached (empty: none).

Returns:

Indexed by the input names, in file order, with the columns status (one of "converted", "converted_no_final_id", "ambiguous", "no_conversion", "not_in_graph", "missing_value", "error"), reason (the text of the conversion’s reason, idtrack.results.REASONS; for "converted" missing, unless the feature had to be read at another release than the dataset’s source release because the graph does not hold it there, or is a copy of another feature made unique by a single-cell tool), ensembl_gene (the gene at the target release when there is exactly one), final_id (the gene’s final-database name: the first in sorted order of gene_names), final_id_alternatives (the gene’s other names, ";"-joined) and own (the input names the gene itself: its stable id, or one of its final-database names, compared without case).

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

output_plan(table, merge, keep_unconverted)[source]

Decide the output features of one dataset from its feature_table() (a pure function of it).

Rules (also in HarmonizeFeatures):

  • A gene reached by exactly one input feature is one output feature named by the gene ("converted", or "converted_no_final_id" when the gene has no final-database id).

  • A gene reached by several input features (“n-to-1”): with merge="sum" one output feature named by the gene whose values are the sum of theirs ("merged"/"merged_no_final_id"); with merge="flag", if exactly one of them names the gene itself (own) it becomes the gene’s feature and the others stay under their input names as "unconverted_merge_partner"; otherwise all stay under their input names as "unconverted_merge_partner" and the gene has no output feature.

  • Every other input feature stays under its input name ("unconverted_ambiguous", "unconverted_no_conversion", "unconverted_not_in_graph", "unconverted_missing_value", "unconverted_error") when keep_unconverted, and is left out otherwise; merge partners are always kept.

  • An input name kept unconverted that equals the name of a converted output feature is renamed "unconverted:<name>".

Parameters:

  • table (DataFrame) – Output of feature_table().

  • merge (str) – "sum" or "flag".

  • keep_unconverted (bool) – Keep the unconverted features (see above).

Returns:

One row per output feature, in the order of its first input feature, indexed by the output name, with the columns sources (list of input positions), query_ids (";"-joined input names), status, reason, ensembl_gene, final_id, final_id_alternatives.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

class HarmonizeFeatures(project_name, data_h5ad_dict, project_local_repository, idtrack_local_repository, to_release, final_database=None, organism=None, snapshot_release=None, from_release_by_dataset=None, from_database_by_dataset=None, api=None, verbosity=2, converted_id_column='converted_id')[source]

Convert the features of several single-cell datasets to one Ensembl release and merge the datasets.

For every dataset, each feature name (Ensembl gene id with or without version, symbol or other external id) is converted with idtrack.API.convert_many() to its Ensembl gene at to_release. The conversion of a dataset depends only on that dataset (its feature names and its from_release_by_dataset and from_database_by_dataset entries), never on the other datasets.

Output features. Each converted gene is one feature, named by the gene id at the target release (with version); its final-database name (default: the organism’s symbol database) is in the column named after the final database. That name is a property of the gene, not of the query: the gene’s ids in the final database at the target release (idtrack.engine.Track.gene_to_database(): read from the gene, no search), the first in sorted order when there are several (the others in "<final database>_alternatives"). A gene without an id in the final database keeps the gene id as its feature name and a missing final-database name (status "converted_no_final_id"): the final-database column never holds an Ensembl id. Which gene a feature is, is decided as Ensembl genes (idtrack.API.convert(): a target in a final database is an id of the gene answered), so a feature whose gene has no name there is that gene, never another gene that has one. Features that are not converted keep their input name; no feature is dropped silently. Every output feature has, in var:

  • "idtrack_status": "converted", "converted_no_final_id", "merged", "merged_no_final_id" (with merge="sum", the sum of several input features), "unconverted_merge_partner" (with merge="flag", an input feature that shares its gene with others), "unconverted_ambiguous" (several genes), "unconverted_no_conversion" (in the graph, but no gene at the target release), "unconverted_not_in_graph", "unconverted_missing_value" (a spelling of a missing value, nan or NA, which is never a gene: decision 81) or "unconverted_error" (the conversion of this feature raised an error that concerns it alone, a search over its budget);

  • "idtrack_reason": why (missing for a plain conversion; the text of the conversion’s reason, idtrack.results.REASONS, for a feature without a conversion; for a feature that the graph does not hold at its dataset’s source release and that was therefore read at another release, that release; for a feature that is another feature of the dataset with a suffix a single-cell tool appends to repeated names, the feature it copies, decision 82);

  • "Query ID": the input name(s), ";"-joined for a merged feature;

  • "matching_ensembl_gene": the gene (also for a merge partner; missing for the other unconverted features).

Several input features of one dataset on one gene (an Ensembl merge, or two aliases): with merge="sum" (right for counts) they become one feature whose values in X and every layer are the sum of theirs; with merge="flag" (default, for normalised data, where a sum has no meaning) the feature that names the gene itself (its stable id or one of its final-database names, ignoring version and case) becomes the gene’s feature, and the others keep their input names with status "unconverted_merge_partner" (if none or several name the gene, all keep their names and the gene has no feature). Rows that a merge sums carry a var value only where all their input features agree (missing otherwise), and varm/varp are left out of a dataset in which features were summed.

An unconverted input name that equals a converted feature’s name (in the dataset, or in another dataset when merging) is renamed "unconverted:<name>", so that converted and unconverted measurements never share a row.

Result cache. The conversions of each dataset are stored in project_local_repository as one JSON file per dataset (written to a temporary file and renamed). A stored file is used only if it was written under the same rules of conversion (idtrack.settings.RULES_VERSION, raised with every change of an answer) for the same graph (its content digest, read from the graph file’s record or from the loaded graph) and the same feature names, organism, final database, target and source release and graph snapshot; an unreadable or mismatching file is recomputed and replaced. Conversions with a graph that records no digest (made in memory) are not cached.

Parameters:

  • project_name (str) – Label used in log messages and cache file names.

  • data_h5ad_dict (dict[str, str]) – {dataset name: path of an .h5ad file}; at least one.

  • project_local_repository (str) – Writable folder for the result cache (created if missing).

  • idtrack_local_repository (str) – idtrack’s local repository holding the graph.

  • to_release (int) – Ensembl release all features are converted to; a release of the graph.

  • final_database (Optional[str]) – Database of the feature names in the output (e.g. "HGNC Symbol"). Defaults to the organism’s first symbol database (idtrack.organisms.SYMBOL_DATABASES: HGNC Symbol for human, MGI Symbol for mouse, VGNC Symbol for pig and the macaques).

  • organism (Optional[str]) – Organism, as an Ensembl species name (e.g. "homo_sapiens") or any query idtrack.API.ensembl_organism() accepts. If None, it is read from the graph files in idtrack_local_repository, which must then hold graphs of exactly one organism.

  • snapshot_release (Optional[int]) – Snapshot release of the graph. If None, the newest graph of the organism in idtrack_local_repository (built by idtrack.API.build()) is used, or the latest Ensembl release of the organism when there is none.

  • from_release_by_dataset (Optional[dict[str, int]]) – The Ensembl release each dataset was annotated with, by dataset name. A dataset with a release is converted with from_release; a feature that the graph does not hold at that release is read where the graph holds it (the rule without a release, below), and its "idtrack_reason" says so. Without a release, each feature is read at the target release if it is active there, else at the latest release in which it is active.

  • from_database_by_dataset (Optional[dict[str, str]]) – The external database the feature names of a dataset are ids of, by dataset name ({"study_a": "HGNC Symbol"}; one of idtrack.API.external_databases()). A dataset with a database is converted with from_database: every feature is read as an id of that database, so a symbol that another database gives to another gene is not a tie, and a feature that is no id of that database (an Ensembl id among symbols) is not converted. Without one, nothing is assumed about where a name comes from: a name that two databases give to two genes stands for both (status "unconverted_ambiguous") when both genes have a name in final_database; a tie is judged among the genes that can be named there, so when only one of the two has a name in it, the feature is converted to that gene. Nothing is inferred from the names on the caller’s behalf.

  • api (Optional[idtrack.API]) – An idtrack.API with the graph already loaded, to use instead of loading the graph again. Without it, the harmonizer loads the graph only if some dataset is not in the result cache, and releases it when the conversions are done.

  • verbosity (Literal[0, 1, 2, 3]) – 0 shows nothing, 1 progress bars, 2 also a summary of each dataset’s conversions (logged at INFO by the "idtrack" loggers; see idtrack.API.configure_logger()), 3 also debug messages. The harmonizer never configures logging itself.

  • converted_id_column (str) – Name of the merged final-database column of unify_multiple_anndatas().

feature_names

The feature names of each dataset, in file order.

Type:

dict[str, list[str]]

matchings

The conversion of each feature of each dataset (results of idtrack.API.convert(), plain data).

Type:

dict[str, list[dict]]

gene_names

Per dataset, the final-database names of each gene reached.

Type:

dict[str, dict[str, list[str]]]

Validate the arguments, read the feature names and convert every feature of every dataset.

Everything that can be checked without the graph is checked before any conversion starts (the arguments, the files, the feature names, the project folder). The conversions then run, or are read from the result cache; this is the long part (minutes for large datasets when nothing is cached).

Parameters:

  • project_name (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • data_h5ad_dict (dict[str, str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • project_local_repository (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • idtrack_local_repository (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • to_release (int) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • final_database (Optional[str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • organism (Optional[str]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • snapshot_release (Optional[int]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • from_release_by_dataset (Optional[dict[str, int]]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • from_database_by_dataset (Optional[dict[str, str]]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • api (Optional[idtrack.API]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • verbosity (Literal[0, 1, 2, 3]) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

  • converted_id_column (str) – See HarmonizeFeatures.

Raises:

  • idtrack.errors.ArgumentTypeError – If a release is not an integer.

  • idtrack.errors.InvalidArgumentError – If verbosity is not 0 to 3; if data_h5ad_dict is empty, names a missing file or a dataset whose feature names are empty, not strings or repeated; if from_release_by_dataset or from_database_by_dataset names an unknown dataset; if a source database is not a string, or to_release is after the graph snapshot; if organism is None and the graphs in idtrack_local_repository do not name exactly one organism; if final_database is None and the organism declares no symbol database. Also the errors of idtrack.API.convert_many() (e.g. a release or database not of the graph).

feature_harmonizer(dataset_name, merge='flag', keep_unconverted=True)[source]

Return one dataset with its features converted (see HarmonizeFeatures for the rules).

The .h5ad file is read completely and never altered. X and every layer get the output features (columns selected, merged ones summed); obs, obsm, obsp and uns are kept as they are; varm and varp are subset to the output features, or left out when features were summed. var holds the columns <final database>, "<final database>_alternatives", "Query ID", "matching_ensembl_gene", "idtrack_status", "idtrack_reason" and then the input’s own columns (an input column with one of those names gets the suffix "_input"; for a merged feature, an input value is kept where all its input features agree and is missing otherwise). raw is dropped with a warning, because its features are not converted.

Parameters:

  • merge (Literal["flag", "sum"]) – How several input features of one gene are handled (default "flag").

  • keep_unconverted (bool) – Keep the features that are not converted, under their input names (default).

Returns:

The harmonised anndata.AnnData, the number of input features and the number of output features.

tuple

unify_multiple_anndatas(features='union', obs_join='outer', obs_columns_to_keep=None, numeric_var_columns=None, numeric_obs_columns=None, handle_anndata_key='handle_anndata', merge='flag', keep_unconverted=True)[source]

Merge the harmonised datasets of data_h5ad_dict into one AnnData.

Each dataset is harmonised with feature_harmonizer() (with merge and keep_unconverted) and all are concatenated along the cells in one anndata.concat(). A feature is the same feature in two datasets when it has the same name: a converted gene id, or the same unconverted input name (an unconverted name equal to another dataset’s converted gene id is renamed "unconverted:<name>" first). By default nothing is lost, and values are never rewritten: text stays text, numbers stay numbers, and where a dataset has no value the result holds a missing value of the column’s kind (NaN for floats and text, pd.NA in a nullable integer or boolean column, NaT for times, a missing category for categoricals), never a placeholder string.

  • Features. "union" (default) keeps every feature of any dataset; a dataset that lacks a feature gets zeros for it in X and in every layer. "intersect" keeps the features present in every dataset.

  • .obs. obs_join="outer" (default) keeps every obs column of any dataset; in the cells of a dataset without the column it is missing (see above; an integer or boolean column becomes the nullable Int/ boolean dtype so that it can hold the missing values). obs_join="inner" keeps only the columns every dataset has. obs_columns_to_keep, if given, selects among the joined columns (in its order); a name that no dataset has, or (with "inner") that not every dataset has, raises ValueError naming it. Columns in numeric_obs_columns are converted to float (missing values allowed); other text columns become categorical (values unchanged). The column handle_anndata_key records the dataset of each cell (categorical, in the order of data_h5ad_dict), and cells are named f"{handle}_{cell}".

  • .var. converted_id_column holds the final-database name of each feature (missing for features without one), "matching_ensembl_gene" its gene. Per dataset: f"{column}_{handle}" for "Query ID", "idtrack_status" and "idtrack_reason" (missing where the dataset lacks the feature). In "union" also f"{converted_id_column}_{handle}" and an integer "intersection" column (1 if the feature is in every dataset, by presence, whatever its name). Every other var column of the inputs is kept: as one column when, for every feature, the datasets that have a value for it agree; otherwise per dataset as f"{column}_{handle}" for each dataset that has it. Columns in numeric_var_columns are converted to float; other text columns become categorical (values unchanged).

  • layers, obsm, obsp, uns. Handled by anndata.concat(): a layer or obsm entry present in every dataset is concatenated (obsp block-diagonally), and an uns entry is kept when it is the same in every dataset. varm, varp and raw are not carried into the merged object.

X keeps the common dtype of the inputs (e.g. float32 stays float32).

Parameters:

  • features (Literal["union", "intersect"]) – How to combine the feature sets (see above).

  • obs_join (Literal["outer", "inner"]) – Which obs columns to keep: of any dataset ("outer") or of every dataset ("inner").

  • obs_columns_to_keep (list[str] | None) – Restrict obs to these joined columns. None keeps all.

  • numeric_var_columns (set[str] | None) – var columns to convert to float.

  • numeric_obs_columns (set[str] | None) – obs columns to convert to float.

  • handle_anndata_key (str) – Name of the obs column that records the dataset of each cell. Defaults to "handle_anndata"; it must not be a column of any dataset.

  • merge (Literal["flag", "sum"]) – See feature_harmonizer().

  • keep_unconverted (bool) – See feature_harmonizer().

Returns:

The merged object; cells in the order of data_h5ad_dict, then of each file.

Return type:

anndata.AnnData

Raises:

InvalidArgumentError – If features, obs_join or merge is not one of its values; if a name of obs_columns_to_keep is not among the joined columns, handle_anndata_key is already an obs column, or a numeric column is absent or holds a value that is not a number; if two cells get the same name; if a generated var column name clashes with an input column.

Building graphs

Building graphs.

Ensembl access (MySQL and HTTPS dumps, REST), the table store, the derived tables, the externals configuration and the graph builder. This is the only part of idtrack that needs pandas, h5py, PyMySQL and PyYAML.

The names are imported on first access.

class GraphMaker(database_manager)[source]

Builds the identifier graph of one organism and keeps it in the local repository.

The graph (idtrack.TheGraph) holds the history of Ensembl gene ids over the releases of the manager’s window, the transcripts and translations of every release linked to their genes, versionless base gene ids, and the identifiers of the selected external databases linked to the Ensembl ids they annotate.

The history is not copied from Ensembl’s mapping_session table unchecked: the releases of every event are validated against the id tables of the releases (which ids exist where), sessions whose recorded releases contradict the tables are corrected, and every correction is logged and recorded in the graph’s record.

A built graph is written as one file whose record says what it is and what built it; get_graph() loads a file only if that record is the graph that is asked for.

Class initialization.

Parameters:

database_manager (DatabaseManager) – Needed to download all necessary tables and data frames. It contains the temporary directory to save the resultant graph.

Raises:

InvalidArgumentError – If the release of database_manager is not the newest release of its window (a graph is the snapshot of the releases first_release to snapshot_release; it is built from the newest of them), or if its genome assembly is not the organism’s default primary assembly of that release (graphs are built on the default primary assembly only; the releases of the other assemblies are in the graph through it).

construct_graph(session_details=False, forms=None, all_external=False)[source]

Build the graph from the tables of the manager.

The steps: the ids of every form at every release (_collect_ids()), the gene history (history()), the Ensembl nodes, the genes that lie outside the reference sequence (_gene_regions()), the relations between the forms (_add_relation_edges()), the identifiers of the external databases (_add_external_edges()), and the versionless base gene ids (_add_base_id_edges()). External identifiers that differ only in letter case are one node, named with the spelling that Ensembl gives at the latest release in which the identifier exists; how each database wrote it at each release is kept beside it (_merge_spellings(), idtrack.TheGraph.spelling()). The nodes and edges are then packed into the graph’s store (_pack()), and the graph’s record says what it is and what built it (idtrack.graph.GraphRecord).

Parameters:

  • session_details (bool) – If True, the history report of the record also lists Ensembl’s mapping sessions with their database names, assemblies and dates (read from the full id-history table). The graph itself is the same.

  • forms (list | None) – The forms to include, a list of ‘gene’, ‘transcript’, ‘translation’ that contains ‘gene’. If None, all forms of the manager.

  • all_external (bool) – If True, every external database of Ensembl is included, not only those selected in the organism’s externals YAML file. The graph becomes much larger and conversions slower.

Returns:

The frozen graph, with its record (idtrack.TheGraph.record).

Raises:

  • ValueError – If the Ensembl ids of the organism carry no versions in some release (such organisms are not supported; raised by the manager when the ids are read, before anything else is done), or if the tables contradict each other (an edge to a node that does not exist, an external table that names an Ensembl id which the primary assembly does not have).

  • HistoryValidationError – If a mapping session cannot be reconciled with the id tables.

Return type:

TheGraph

create_file_name(session_details=False, forms=None, all_external=False)[source]

Return the path of the graph file in the manager’s local repository.

Parameters:

  • session_details (bool) – See construct_graph().

  • forms (list[str] | None) – See construct_graph().

  • all_external (bool) – See construct_graph().

Returns:

Absolute file path; see idtrack.graph.files.graph_file_path().

Return type:

str

get_graph(session_details=False, create_even_if_exist=False, save_after_calculation=True, *, forms=None, all_external=False)[source]

Load the graph from the local repository, or build it.

A graph file is loaded only if its record is the graph that is asked for: organism, primary assembly, release window, snapshot release, forms, the selection of external databases and the organism table. A file that holds another graph under the expected name is an error, not a silent substitute and not a silent rebuild of several hours.

Parameters:

  • session_details (bool) – See construct_graph().

  • create_even_if_exist (bool) – Build the graph even if a file exists. The new graph replaces the file (unless save_after_calculation is False).

  • save_after_calculation (bool) – Write a newly built graph to the local repository.

  • forms (list[str] | None) – See construct_graph().

  • all_external (bool) – See construct_graph().

Returns:

The frozen graph.

Raises:

GraphMismatchError – If the file in the local repository is not the graph asked for, or unreadable. The message names the differences; create_even_if_exist=True replaces the file.

TheGraph

graph_identity(session_details=False, forms=None, all_external=False)[source]

Return the fields of a record that say which graph this maker builds; a loaded file must have the same.

Computed from the manager, the organism table and the externals YAML file only (no table is read).

Parameters:

  • forms (list[str] | None) – See construct_graph().

The fields idtrack.graph.record.IDENTITY_FIELDS as JSON values: organism, primary_assembly, first_release and window_end (the window; None for no limit), snapshot_release, forms, session_details, all_external, externals_fingerprint (the databases selected per form, assembly and release, as far as the selection takes effect: inside the window and inside the releases the organism table gives the assembly) and organism_table_fingerprint (the assemblies of the organism with their release ranges and order).
