dict

graph_releases()[source]

Return the releases the graph covers: every release of the organism in the window, up to the snapshot.

The snapshot is the release of the manager, the newest release of the primary assembly in the window.

Returns:

Releases, ascending.

Return type:

list[int]

history(database_manager, session_details=False)[source]

Build the history edges of one form from the id tables of the releases and Ensembl’s id-history table.

The id tables say which <id>.<version> exists in which release (each release from the assembly that serves it in the backbone; _timeline()). From them come the edges of an id with itself (_self_history()): <id>.Void → <id>.<v> at its first appearance, <id>.<v> → <id>.<w> at a change of version, <id>.<v> → <id>.Retired when it disappears, <id>.Retired → <id>.<v> when it comes back, and a self-loop to infinity on every id of the last release (_snapshot_loops()).

Ensembl’s stable_id_event table says which id passed into which other id (and which id was re-mapped onto itself with a score below 1, or onto itself in a session that also maps it to or from another id), per mapping session (_events_and_weights()). The releases of a session are not taken from mapping_session: an event from A to B belongs to the pair of consecutive releases at which A exists in the first and B in the second. For every session the pair that most of its events fit is determined; it replaces the recorded pair where the two differ (Ensembl’s pig session 106 to 107 is recorded as 106 to 104; sessions over a gap such as rhesus 50 to 52 belong to 51 to 52). An event whose old version did not exist at the session’s old release, while its stable id did, is placed with the version the id had there; an event that does not fit its session’s pair otherwise is placed at the nearest pair it fits; an event that fits no pair, or whose ids are in no id table, contradicts the tables and is left out (_place_sessions()). All of it is counted in the report. The edges are put in a deterministic order, keyed and checked against the id tables (_key_and_validate()).

Parameters:

  • database_manager (DatabaseManager) – The manager of the form, at the snapshot release.

  • session_details (bool) – Read the full id-history table, whose session metadata then goes into the report (True), or the narrow one.

Returns:

The edges as (source, target, old_release, new_release, weight, key) tuples (new_release is infinity on the self-loops of the last release), sorted, and the report for the record: the sessions with recorded and used release pairs and their counts, and the corrections.

Raises:

  • HistoryValidationError – If the events of a session fit no pair of consecutive releases, fit several pairs equally well without the recorded one among them, if an event fits two pairs equally near its session’s pair, or if the id-history table does not reach back to the first release of the graph although Ensembl’s mapping_session does (a table computed for another release window).

  • ValueError – If an id of the last release is missing from the backbone, or if the ids of a release carry no versions (raised by the manager, see construct_graph()).

Return type:

tuple[list[tuple], dict[str, Any]]

static load_graph(local_repository, organism, snapshot_release, first_release=None, *, session_details=False, forms=None, all_external=False, graph_settings=None)[source]

Load a stored graph without a DatabaseManager and without any network access.

The file is found by its name (idtrack.graph.files.graph_file_path()) and checked against what is asked for, as in get_graph(): organism, primary assembly, release window, forms, the selection of external databases (the externals YAML of the local repository, else the one shipped with the package) and the organism table.

Parameters:

  • local_repository (str) – Folder that holds the graph file.

  • organism (str) – Organism name, e.g. homo_sapiens.

  • snapshot_release (int) – Last release of the graph’s window (snapshot_release of API.build).

  • first_release (int | None) – First release of the window; by default the first release of the organism in the organism table (idtrack.organisms.first_release()), as API.build.

  • session_details (bool) – See construct_graph().

  • forms (list[str] | None) – See construct_graph().

  • all_external (bool) – See construct_graph().

  • graph_settings (GraphSettings | None) – The caches and hyper-connectivity threshold of the graph.

Returns:

The frozen graph.

Raises:

  • GraphFileError – If the local repository has no such graph file (build it with get_graph()).

  • GraphMismatchError – If the file holds another graph than the one asked for.

  • UnknownReleaseError – If no assembly of the organism has snapshot_release.

Return type:

TheGraph

class DatabaseManager(organism, form, local_repository, release=None, first_release=None, snapshot_release=None, store_raw_always=True, assembly=None)[source]

Manage retrieval, preprocessing, and storage of Ensembl Core and related external datasets.

The DatabaseManager centralizes all low-level operations required for ID-track analyses, including discovering which Ensembl releases are available for a given organism/assembly, downloading the corresponding MySQL tables, normalizing column names, persisting raw and processed files under a local cache directory, and orchestrating auxiliary look-ups to third-party resources via ExternalDatabases. By funnelling every data-access path through a single object the wider package gains:

  • Stable, reproducible builds - every graph, lookup table, or ID-history file is anchored to the exact Ensembl release, genome assembly, and form (gene, transcript, translation, …) with which the manager was configured.

  • Transparent caching - expensive downloads happen once; every table is kept in a file of its own in the local repository (tables_directory), written atomically and named by everything it depends on (release, form, externals selection), so a table computed for other parameters is never served.

  • Versioned ids only - idtrack follows <id>.<version> through the releases. A release whose Ensembl ids carry no versions (some organisms, e.g. S. cerevisiae) is refused where its id table is read (create_ids()), with an error that says so: no table is made up for it.

Key public methods/attributes

  • available_releases() — list releases of the assembly within the window.

  • change_release() — a new manager for another Ensembl release (likewise change_form(), change_assembly(), change_release_auto_assembly()).

  • get_table() — a raw Ensembl table (stored after the first download); download_table() fetches one without storing it.

  • get_db() — a derived table (ids, history, relations, cross references).

  • create_external_all() — the cross references of every assembly the externals YAML enables for the release.

  • organism, form, release, assembly — core configuration knobs, surfaced for quick inspection.

A manager’s configuration does not change after construction; the change_* methods return new managers. Use the built-in __str__() for a concise, human-readable dump of that state.

Initialize a DatabaseManager for a specific organism, release, and assembly.

param organism:

Canonical species name in Ensembl schema (e.g. "homo_sapiens"); one of idtrack.organisms.supported_organisms(), otherwise idtrack.errors.UnknownOrganismError is raised.

type organism:

str

param form:

Biological entity level of interest—one of "gene", "transcript", "translation", …—governing which stable-ID columns will be expected downstream.

type form:

str

param local_repository:

Directory of the cached tables (tables_directory, one HDF5 file per table), the saved index of Ensembl’s dumps and the graphs. It must exist and be readable; it must be writable only when a table has to be computed and stored (a read-only repository serves what it holds).

type local_repository:

str

param release:

Target Ensembl release number. If None the most recent release available for assembly is selected automatically.

type release:

Optional[int]

param first_release:

Earliest release to include when building cross-release ID histories. Defaults to the first release of the organism in the organism table (idtrack.organisms.first_release(), over all its assemblies), the same default as idtrack.API uses.

type first_release:

Optional[int]

param snapshot_release:

Latest release to include when building histories. None (the default) or np.inf disables the upper bound and includes all newer releases.

type snapshot_release:

Optional[int | float]

param store_raw_always:

When True (default) raw Ensembl tables are stored in the repository after their download; when False they are not, and every derived table that needs them downloads them again.

type store_raw_always:

bool

param assembly:

Assembly key of the organism table (idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE), as an integer of any integer type, an integral float or a string of digits (idtrack.organisms.assembly_key()). This selects the primary assembly used for data access (e.g. 38 = human GRCh38, 39 = mouse GRCm39, 111 = pig Sscrofa11.1, 10 = rhesus Mmul_10). The key usually equals the code in core schema names (<organism>_core_<release>_<code>); see the table’s DbSuffix. If omitted, the highest-priority assembly for organism is used. If release is provided, the selection is restricted to assemblies that actually contain that release; otherwise to assemblies with a release inside the first_release/snapshot_release window.

type assembly:

Optional[int]

raises ValueError:

If form is not in the supported list, local_repository fails basic path/read/write checks, or the Ensembl access mode (IDTRACK_ENSEMBL_ACCESS / idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.access) is invalid.

raises RuntimeError:

If internal port/release configuration is inconsistent.

raises UnknownOrganismError:

If organism is not in the organism table (idtrack.organisms.supported_organisms()).

assembly_chain(earlier, later)[source]

Return Ensembl’s mapping of one assembly of the organism onto another, where Ensembl publishes one.

Ensembl’s chain file of the pair (<name>_to_<name>.chain.gz in the assembly_chain folder of a release, idtrack.build.assembly_chain) is looked for in the folders of the window’s releases, newest first, downloaded once into the local repository and kept there (raw downloads are never removed).

Parameters:

  • earlier (int) – The assembly key of the assembly mapped.

  • later (int) – The assembly key of the assembly it is mapped onto.

Returns:

The aligned blocks (idtrack.build.assembly_chain.BLOCK_COLUMNS) and what a graph’s record says of the file (from, to, release, sha256, file); None where Ensembl publishes no such file in those folders.

Return type:

tuple | None

property available_releases: list[int]

Return Ensembl releases that are both reachable and within the window.

Availability is read from the cached, multi-port aware core index built by _get_core_db_index() (the union of releases over the ports), filtered against first_release / snapshot_release, sorted in ascending order, and cached for the lifetime of this DatabaseManager instance. The resulting list represents releases that can safely be queried and cached locally, guaranteeing reproducible downstream analyses.

Returns:

Sorted release numbers satisfying reachability and window constraints.

Return type:

list[int]

property available_releases_all_assemblies: list[int]

Return all Ensembl releases that have a core database of at least one configured assembly.

For clean-handoff species (e.g. mouse: 37 → 38 → 39), no single assembly spans the full release history. Graph construction and YAML template generation therefore need a release catalogue that is the union over all assemblies configured for organism in idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE.

The list is filtered by the manager’s first_release / snapshot_release window and cached for the lifetime of this DatabaseManager instance. Every assembly’s index must be complete: if one cannot be built (Ensembl does not answer), the error is raised instead of leaving that assembly’s releases out.

Returns:

Sorted release numbers available for at least one configured assembly.

Return type:

list[int]

change_assembly(assembly, last_possible_release=False)[source]

Clone the manager while targeting a new genome assembly (e.g. GRCh38 → GRCh37).

Genome assemblies are identified by the integer keys of idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE (38 for GRCh38, 37 for GRCh37, 39 for GRCm39, 111 for Sscrofa11.1, 1 for rhesus MMUL_1, …). When last_possible_release is True the method automatically picks the most recent Ensembl release that still provides MySQL dumps for the requested assembly, ensuring compatibility. All other settings are copied verbatim.

Parameters:

  • assembly (int) – Assembly code configured under organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE for this manager’s organism.

  • last_possible_release (bool) – When True override release with the newest version available for assembly. Defaults to False.

Returns:

New manager tied to the requested assembly (and possibly a recalculated release).

Return type:

DatabaseManager

change_form(form)[source]

Clone the manager while switching the biological form of interest.

A “form” denotes the identifier namespace to track—gene, transcript, translation, etc. This method preserves every other configuration knob (organism, release, assembly, cache directory, ignore windows, …) and returns a brand-new instance so that the original object remains unaffected.

Parameters:

form (str) – Target form/namespace recognised by __init__(). Typical values are "gene", "transcript", or "translation".

Returns:

An independent manager identical to self except for form.

DatabaseManager

change_release(release)[source]

Produce a new manager that targets a different Ensembl release.

The returned instance inherits organism, form, assembly, and all caching parameters, but points every subsequent query (MySQL, FTP, or REST) to release. This is the recommended way to traverse releases in scripted analyses without mutating objects in-place.

Parameters:

release (int) – Desired Ensembl release number (e.g. 111). Must be available for the current genome assembly, otherwise idtrack.errors.UnknownReleaseError is raised.

Returns:

Fresh manager initialised for release.

DatabaseManager

change_release_auto_assembly(release)[source]

Clone the manager for release while inferring a compatible genome assembly.

Unlike change_release(), this helper allows assembly to change when the requested release is not present in the current assembly (common for clean-handoff species). Assembly inference follows the same priority rules as __init__() with assembly=None: pick the highest-priority configured assembly that contains the requested release.

Parameters:

release (int) – Desired Ensembl release number.

Returns:

Fresh manager initialised for release with an inferred assembly.

Return type:

DatabaseManager

create_assembly_exceptions()[source]

Return Ensembl’s assembly exceptions of the release: which region of the reference each other sequence takes.

An assembly patch, a haplotype (an alternative locus) or a pseudoautosomal region is, in Ensembl’s core database, a sequence region of its own whose bases stand for a region of the reference sequence: the table assembly_exception gives, per such region, its bases (seq_region_start to seq_region_end), the region of the reference they stand for (exc_seq_region_id from exc_seq_region_start to exc_seq_region_end) and the type of the exception (exc_type: PATCH_FIX, PATCH_NOVEL, HAP, PAR). A gene on a patch or a haplotype is a copy of, or an alternative to, a gene of that reference region (idtrack.graph.genes.relation()); the Y copy of a gene of a pseudoautosomal region lies at the place of its X gene (idtrack.TheGraph.repeated_regions). An LRG record has no exception.

The table is a function of five raw tables of the release (assembly_exception, seq_region, coord_system, seq_region_attrib and attrib_type).

Returns:

One row per exception: seq_region (the name of the region), start, end, type, ref_region (the name of the reference region), ref_start, ref_end, ref_kind (its kind, one of idtrack.graph.genes.PLACE_KINDS), sorted.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_available_databases()[source]

List the core databases of the organism’s configured assemblies, each within its release range.

The names come from the core-database index of every assembly in the organism table (_get_core_db_index()): databases named with the assembly’s DbSuffix (patch letters included, e.g. homo_sapiens_core_54_36p) whose release lies in the assembly’s ReleaseRange and at or above release 48. The index merges the live MySQL catalogue (where its ports are usable) with the HTTPS dump listings, so the list is the same whichever way Ensembl is reached. Core databases of assemblies that the table does not declare, or outside their ranges, are not listed. An assembly for which no database is found contributes nothing; a failure to build an index raises.

An invalid Ensembl access mode raises its own ValueError here (see idtrack.build.ensembl_access.ensembl_access_mode()).

Returns:

One column named "available_databases", sorted.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_database_content()[source]

Retrieve external-database metadata for every assembly, release, and form.

The helper iterates over every genome assembly configured for the current organism in idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE, every available Ensembl release for each assembly, and every identifier form supported by the package, downloading the external_database table for each combination. The resulting frames are concatenated, enriched with assembly, release, form, and organism columns, and returned to the caller.

Returns:

External-database relationships augmented with assembly, release, form, and organism

columns.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_external_all(all_external=False)[source]

Download and collate cross-reference mappings from every supported genome assembly.

The manager cycles through every genome assembly recognised for the current organism (ordered by idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE), fetches either the filtered external_relevant mapping table (when all_external=False) or the full external mapping table (when all_external=True) for each via get_db(), labels every row with its source assembly, and concatenates the tables, keeping one copy of every unique (release, graph_id, id_db, name_db, ensembl_identity, xref_identity, assembly) combination (duplicates are resolved within each assembly only). It bypasses the get_db() caching layer and never writes the result to the local repository.

Parameters:

all_external (bool) – If False (default), restrict results to databases enabled in the externals YAML configuration (external_relevant). If True, include all external databases of Ensembl (external).

Returns:

The cross-reference table with the columns release, graph_id, id_db, name_db, ensembl_identity, xref_identity, is_label and assembly.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_external_db(filter_mode)[source]

Retrieve Ensembl-external-ID relationships and/or database statistics.

This consolidates a complex SQL join—spanning Ensembl core tables gene, transcript, translation and the cross-reference tables xref, object_xref, identity_xref, external_db, and external_synonym—into a single pandas dataframe. It enables downstream analyses such as mapping Ensembl gene models to UniProt, RefSeq, or CCDS identifiers, or summarising which external sources are represented in a given Ensembl release. The result type and granularity are controlled by filter_mode, allowing either the raw relationship rows or a per-database count to be returned.

The query executed is conceptually equivalent to the (simplified) MySQL statement below, though the actual SQL is constructed programmatically for flexibility and performance:

SELECT g.stable_id, t.stable_id, tr.stable_id, x.dbprimary_acc, edb.db_name, es.synonym, ix.*
FROM gene g
JOIN transcript t USING (gene_id)
JOIN translation tr USING (transcript_id)
JOIN object_xref ox ON (g.gene_id = ox.ensembl_id AND ox.ensembl_object_type = "Gene")
JOIN xref x ON (ox.xref_id = x.xref_id)
LEFT JOIN external_db edb ON (x.external_db_id = edb.external_db_id)
LEFT JOIN identity_xref ix ON (ox.object_xref_id = ix.object_xref_id)
LEFT JOIN external_synonym es ON (x.xref_id = es.xref_id)
LIMIT 10;

When tighter genomic scoping is required the gene table can be prefixed with coord_system and seq_region:

FROM coord_system cs
JOIN seq_region  sr USING (coord_system_id)
JOIN gene        g  USING (seq_region_id)

You can experiment interactively against the public Ensembl MySQL mirror:

mysql --user=anonymous --host=ensembldb.ensembl.org -D homo_sapiens_core_105_38 -A
# Schema reference:
# https://m.ensembl.org/info/docs/api/core/core_schema.html
Parameters:

filter_mode (str) –

Controls both the row subset and the output schema. Must be one of:

  • "all" - return every mapping found in MySQL, no post-filtering applied.

  • "relevant" - return only mappings whose external database is marked Include: true in the

    ExternalDatabases.give_list_for_case() YAML configuration.

  • "database" - return a two-column summary (name_db, count) for all external databases

    (the content of the externals template: what a YAML can select).

  • "relevant-database" - as above, but restricted to databases flagged Include: true.

    The counts are of the databases’ cross references: the genes’ display names, which a graph holds whatever the YAML selects (_with_display_names()), are no entry a YAML selects and are not counted. The special values "relevant" and "relevant-database" implicitly consult the cached external_inst to honour the user’s curated allow-list.

Returns:

  • For "all" / "relevant" - seven-column frame

    ["release", "graph_id", "id_db", "name_db", "ensembl_identity", "xref_identity", "is_label"] holding one row per Ensembl→external identifier edge. graph_id is the Ensembl stable ID (+version), the two identity columns store Smith-Waterman percent identities (float16) for QC, and is_label says whether the row is a label (a display name) rather than an accession.

  • For "database" / "relevant-database" - two-column frame

    ["name_db", "count"] giving the number of rows of each external database (most rows first, ties by name). count is an int64.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

  • ValueError – If filter_mode is not one of the accepted literals or if the YAML allow-list claims a database that is absent from the retrieved mappings—indicating the configuration and MySQL data are out of sync.

  • EnsemblSchemaError – If identity_xref lacks columns other than its identity columns.

Notes

Synonym handling - any synonym brought in from external_synonym is prefixed with ids.SYNONYM_PREFIX, and its name_db is likewise prefixed so that synonym nodes remain distinguishable during graph building. Caching - this method always computes; get_db() stores and reuses its results (external, external_database, and external_relevant keyed by the enabled databases). The raw tables it reads are stored by get_table(). Restriction first - with relevant the raw tables are restricted to the enabled databases before the join (identical result, a fraction of the memory). External ids and synonyms are stripped of surrounding white space; ids that are empty after it are dropped. The rows are in a total order (database, Ensembl id, external id, identities).

create_gene_region()[source]

Tell for every gene of the release where it lies, and whether that is on the reference sequence.

Ensembl annotates genes on the chromosomes and scaffolds of an assembly (its reference sequence) and also on sequence regions beside it: alternative loci (haplotypes), assembly patches and LRG records. A gene on such a region is a copy of, or an alternative to, a gene of the reference sequence and has a stable id of its own. The core database marks these regions with the attribute NON_REFERENCE_ATTRIBUTE (seq_region_attrib joined to attrib_type), in every release and for every kind of region; the table assembly_exception lists only the patches and haplotypes among them (not the LRG records), so it does not say which genes lie outside the reference sequence; it says which region of the reference a patch or a haplotype stands for (create_assembly_exceptions()).

The place of a gene is its sequence region (by name), its start and end (1-based, inclusive, as Ensembl counts) and its strand on the assembly of the release, and what the region is (its kind, one of idtrack.graph.genes.PLACE_KINDS): the mitochondrial genome where the region carries MITOCHONDRIAL_ATTRIBUTE, else a chromosome where its coordinate system is CHROMOSOME_COORD_SYSTEM or the region carries KARYOTYPE_ATTRIBUTE, else a scaffold (or another sequence below a chromosome).

The table is a function of five raw tables of the release (gene with its sequence region and place, seq_region, coord_system, seq_region_attrib and attrib_type) and of the gene ids (idsraw_gene).

Returns:

One row per gene of the release: gene_stable_id, gene_version (as in the ids table of the gene form), non_reference (True for a gene on a region outside the reference sequence; a release whose core database defines no such attribute or marks no region has False throughout), seq_region (the region’s name), start, end, strand and kind.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If a gene of the id table has no sequence region in the gene table.

create_id_history(narrow)[source]

Retrieve historical relationships between successive Ensembl stable IDs.

Build a cross-release lineage table mapping every obsolete ID version to its immediate successor for the configured organism and form, over every mapping session that the release’s tables record (all earlier releases; get_db() restricts it to the manager’s window). The information is assembled from the Core tables stable_id_event and mapping_session and then normalised so that all identifiers follow the canonical <stable_id>.<version> convention. Downstream graph-construction utilities depend on this table to reconstruct how genes, transcripts, or translations evolve across Ensembl releases.

Parameters:

narrow (bool) – If True drop auxiliary columns (mapping session metadata, assembly labels, creation timestamps, etc.) to minimise on-disk footprint; otherwise return the full schema for exploratory analyses.

Returns:

Seven-column table with the following fields, ordered as listed—

  • old_stable_id - obsolete identifier (empty string for “birth” events).

  • old_version - version number paired with old_stable_id.

  • new_stable_id - successor identifier (empty string for “retirement” events).

  • new_version - version paired with new_stable_id.

  • score - homology score reported by Ensembl (NaN if unavailable).

  • old_release - Ensembl release where the old identifier last appeared.

  • new_release - release where the new identifier first appeared.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If the identifier delimiter idtrack.ids.ID_VERSION_DELIMITER is found inside any *_stable_id field, indicating malformed input.

create_ids(form)[source]

Retrieve and normalise raw Ensembl identifier records for the requested molecular form.

This method pulls the appropriate MySQL table(s) for form, copes with schema differences across Ensembl releases (e.g. the historical *_stable_id split tables), coerces data types, and standardises column names so that downstream graph-building steps all consume the same shape. Every id must carry a version (DatabaseManager._require_versions()): a release whose ids have none, or only some, is refused here, so no derived table exists for it.

Parameters:

form (str) – Target molecular form - "gene", "transcript", or "translation". Anything else triggers a ValueError.

Returns:

A de-duplicated, index-reset table whose columns depend on form:

  • gene - gene_id, gene_stable_id, gene_version

  • transcript - transcript_id, gene_id, transcript_stable_id, transcript_version

  • translation - translation_id, transcript_id, translation_stable_id, translation_version

All ID columns are int64 except the *_stable_id strings; version columns are int64.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If ids of the release carry no version (organisms without versioned ids are not supported).

create_relation_current()[source]

Build a current-release gene-transcript-translation mapping table.

The routine fetches the raw stable-ID/​version tables for genes, transcripts and translations via DatabaseManager.get_db(), merges them into a single wide frame, and then delegates to DatabaseManager._create_relation_helper() to harmonise version columns and compress the information into three canonical node labels ("<stable_id>.<version>"). The resulting mapping is the authoritative per-release link between molecular forms and is consumed by downstream graph-building utilities such as idtrack.GraphMaker.construct_graph().

Returns:

Three columns—gene, transcript, and translation—with one row per transcript. The translation column may contain empty strings where non-coding transcripts have no peptide. All data are UTF-8 strings; duplicates are removed and the index is reset.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

create_release_id()[source]

Return deduplicated stable-identifier/version pairs for the current form and release.

Raw identifiers are fetched via DatabaseManager.get_db(), trimmed to the canonical columns, and sanity-checked. Two integrity rules are enforced: (1) the delimiter idtrack.ids.ID_VERSION_DELIMITER must not appear inside any stable identifier, and (2) every stable identifier must be unique after deduplication. Violations raise idtrack.errors.TableFormatError.

Returns:

Two-column dataframe [{form}_stable_id, {form}_version] with duplicates removed.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If the delimiter is present inside any stable identifier or if identifiers are not unique after deduplication.

database_filing()[source]

Return which of Ensembl’s database names each database the externals YAML selects holds (decision 104).

The selected databases are the (form, name) pairs the YAML enables anywhere (any assembly or release; a synonym’s name by its entry’s). The links of every release of the window are read on the assembly that serves it (_release_links()) and compared between adjacent releases (idtrack.build.continuity. database_filing()). Computed once per process and window; a graph holds what it found (idtrack.graph.GraphRecord.database_names).

Returns:

The names and where they go.

Return type:

idtrack.build.continuity.Filing

download_table(table_key, usecols=None)[source]

Download a raw Ensembl MySQL table and return it as a DataFrame.

When the release is on the live Ensembl MySQL service and its port is usable (see idtrack.build.ensembl_access: the port answered its probe and the access mode is not "https"), the table is selected from the core schema with a server-side cursor (rows are streamed, not held twice); otherwise it is read from Ensembl’s HTTPS dumps (_download_table_from_ftp()). Both routes give the same rows with the same column types: columns of text types (character, enumeration, date and time) are text, the others numbers. Only a failure to reach the MySQL server makes the HTTPS route take over (with a warning that names the cause); a query or data error is raised. Public code is expected to call DatabaseManager.get_table(), which wraps this helper with caching.

Parameters:

  • table_key (str) – Name of the raw table as it appears in the remote Ensembl database (e.g. 'gene', 'mapping_session', 'xref'). Must exist in the schema returned by DatabaseManager.mysql_database().

  • usecols (Optional[list[str]]) – Sequence of column names to project; None retrieves the entire table. Column order is preserved. An empty list is treated the same as None.

Returns:

A frame containing the requested columns in the exact order supplied via

usecols (or all columns if usecols is None). Index is monotonic and zero-based.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

  • EnsemblSchemaError – If the release has no table table_key, or the table lacks an element of usecols (idtrack.errors.EnsemblSchemaError).

  • ValueError – If the query returns text that cannot be decoded.

Notes

If the HTTPS dumps cannot be read, idtrack.EnsemblDownloadError propagates.

property external_inst: ExternalDatabases

Instantiate and cache an ExternalDatabases helper for this manager.

The instance mirrors the configuration of the surrounding DatabaseManager—organism, Ensembl release, identifier form, local repository path, and genome assembly—so that all interactions with external data sources remain consistent throughout the session. Because the property is backed by functools.cached_property, the helper is created exactly once and reused on subsequent accesses, eliminating redundant network or file-system look-ups.

Returns:

A lazily created, configuration-matched helper object.

Return type:

ExternalDatabases

get_db(table_key, create_even_if_exist=False, save_after_calculation=True)[source]

Return a derived table, from the repository or computed.

Every stored table is kept in a file of its own whose name carries everything the table depends on, so a table computed for one window or externals selection is never served for another:

  • external (all cross references of the form), external_database (row counts per database): keyed by release and form.

  • external_relevant: the rows of the databases the externals YAML enables for this form, assembly and release; keyed by release, form and the sorted list of those databases (its digest in the file name, the list itself in the file, checked on read). external_relevant-database counts its rows (not stored).

  • idhistory and idhistory_narrow: Ensembl’s id history of the release, stored for every mapping session the release records (keyed by release and form) and restricted on reading to the sessions whose old_release lies in the manager’s window.

  • relationcurrent: gene, transcript and translation node names per transcript; keyed by release.

  • Not stored, because they are cheap functions of stored tables: idsraw_<form> (raw ids of form, create_ids()), ids (ids and versions of the manager’s form, create_release_id()), generegion (which genes of the release lie outside the reference sequence, create_gene_region()), assemblyexception (which region of the reference each patch, haplotype and pseudoautosomal region stands for, create_assembly_exceptions()). The content of Ensembl’s external databases and the list of the available ones are methods of their own (create_database_content(), create_available_databases()).

Parameters:

  • table_key (str) – One of the indicators above.

  • create_even_if_exist (bool) – Compute a stored table again and replace the stored copy.

  • save_after_calculation (bool) – Store a computed table (ignored for the tables that are not stored).

Returns:

The requested table.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If table_key is not one of the indicators above.

get_table(table_key, usecols=None, create_even_if_exist=False, save_after_calculation=True)[source]

Return a raw Ensembl table of the manager’s release, from the repository or downloaded.

The table is read from its file in tables_directory if one exists (one file per table, release and column set); otherwise it is downloaded (download_table()) and, if save_after_calculation, stored. A raw table depends only on the release’s core database, so it is shared by every manager of the assembly whatever its form or window.

Parameters:

  • table_key (str) – Name of the MySQL table (e.g. "gene", "xref", "mapping_session").

  • usecols (list[str] | None) – Column subset to retrieve. None (default) selects all columns.

  • create_even_if_exist (bool) – Download the table even if it is stored, and replace the stored copy.

  • save_after_calculation (bool) – Store a downloaded table.

Returns:

The requested raw table, its columns in the order of usecols when given, otherwise in

the schema’s order.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

ValueError – If usecols is an empty list or not a list.

id_ver_from_df(table)[source]

Assemble fully qualified node names from a stable-ID / version DataFrame.

This convenience routine converts a two-column frame—usually produced by DatabaseManager.get_db() with the ids form—into the canonical node labels used throughout ID-track graphs (e.g. ENSG00000000001.1). It first validates that the input columns match self._identifiers (typically ["gene_stable_id", "gene_version"] or analogous for the current form), then joins them with idtrack.ids.join_columns().

Parameters:

table (pandas.DataFrame) – Two-column frame containing the stable identifiers and their Ensembl version numbers. The column order and names must exactly match self._identifiers; otherwise an exception is raised.

Returns:

Ordered list where each element is "<ID>.<version>"; for a row

without version (the empty id of a transcript that has no translation) the id itself.

Return type:

list[str]

Raises:

ValueError – If table does not contain the expected column names stored in self._identifiers.

label_names()[source]

Return the name of every database’s label rows in the manager’s window (label_names_of_databases()).

Read from the external_db table of every release of every assembly of the organism in the window (small tables, read once per window and process).

Returns:

{db_name: name of its label rows}.

Return type:

dict[str, str]

property mysql_database: str

Return the canonical Ensembl Core schema name for the current organism, release, and assembly.

The schema naming convention is deterministic:

{organism}_core_{release}_{DbSuffix}[<patch>]

where DbSuffix is the assembly’s core-database code (idtrack.organisms.db_suffix(), usually the assembly key itself).

For multi-port assemblies (e.g. sus_scrofa assembly 102), the port is selected in __init__() using _get_core_db_index(). Once the release is validated to exist on that chosen port, the schema name itself does not require another server-side discovery query.

Returns:

Schema name like "homo_sapiens_core_111_38".

Return type:

str

Raises:

ValueError – If the current release is not available for this (organism, assembly) pair.

one_gene_only_names()[source]

Return the database names of the accessions and labels of ONE_GENE_ONLY in the window.

A database whose gene names are derived from one of them (rules_database(): miRBase_gene_name) is judged with it.

Return type:

set[str]

renamed_label_names()[source]

Return the names that Ensembl gives a database’s labels in the window and idtrack does not, with idtrack’s.

The same holds for their synonyms, with the synonym prefix. A name that is also a database’s own name (db_name) is not listed (it names that database’s accessions), nor is a name Ensembl gave the labels of several databases.

Returns:

{name Ensembl used: name of the label rows}.

Return type:

dict[str, str]

table_digests()[source]

Return {file name: content SHA-256} of every table stored for this organism and assembly.

The digests identify the tables’ content (idtrack.build.tables.read_table_digest()), so that a graph can record what it was built from.

Returns:

Sorted by file name; empty if nothing is stored.

Return type:

dict[str, str]

table_path(name, release=None)[source]

Return the file of a cached table.

Parameters:

  • release (int | None) – Release of the table; the manager’s release by default.

Returns:

<tables_directory>/ens<release>_<name>.h5.

Return type:

str

Folder of this organism’s and assembly’s cached tables

class ExternalDatabases(organism, release, form, local_repository, assembly)[source]

Manage third-party metadata for Ensembl entities through YAML side-car files.

This helper encapsulates everything related to the external (i.e. non-Ensembl) databases that can be linked to a given organism, genome assembly, release, and biological form (gene / transcript / translation). Examples of such resources include ArrayExpress, RefSeq, Uniprot, HGNC, and dozens of smaller annotation providers. Rather than hard-coding those relationships, the wider ID-Track toolkit stores them in a human-readable YAML file that lives next to the local data cache managed by idtrack.build.DatabaseManager.

The YAML workflow is:

  1. create_template_yaml() enumerates every known combination and writes a template where each entry is marked Include: false.

  2. A user (or an automated post-processing step) reviews the template, toggling Include to true for the resources they need.

  3. The modified YAML is saved under local_repository; subsequent calls to load_modified_yaml() return it as a plain dict for downstream logic.

  4. Every file is checked when it is read (validate_externals_yaml(): boolean Include, assembly keys and releases that the organism table allows), and validate_yaml_file_up_to_date() raises ExternalsReleaseNotCoveredError if the manager’s release is not listed at all (extend_modified_yaml() adds new releases).

  5. Utility helpers such as give_list_for_case() expose convenient filtered views—e.g. all databases that should be downloaded for the current form, or all releases supported by assembly 38.

In short, ExternalDatabases provides a single, version-controlled “contract” describing which third-party tables belong in an ID-track run, while granting users explicit opt-in control over optional resources.

Instantiate a YAML controller tied to a specific organism, release, and assembly.

The constructor mirrors the core configuration of idtrack.build.DatabaseManager so that both objects operate on the exact same coordinate system. No I/O is performed at construction time; paths are merely recorded, and loggers are configured. Heavy-weight actions—such as scanning the cache for existing YAMLs or writing new ones—happen lazily when the corresponding methods are called.

Parameters:

  • organism (str) – Canonical Ensembl species identifier in snake_case (e.g. "homo_sapiens"), exactly as in idtrack.organisms.supported_organisms().

  • release (int) – Target Ensembl release number (e.g. 110). Must correspond to a release that actually exists for organism and assembly.

  • form (str) – Entity level—"gene", "transcript", or "translation". Any other value raises ValueError in higher-level validation.

  • local_repository (str) – Writable directory where YAML files and downloads are cached. The directory need not pre-exist; if missing, most public methods will attempt to create it.

  • assembly (int) – Assembly key of idtrack.organisms.ORGANISM_TABLE (e.g. 38 = human GRCh38, 37 = human GRCh37, 39 = mouse GRCm39, 111 = pig Sscrofa11.1, 10 = rhesus Mmul_10). The YAML’s assembly keys are these keys. Used to disambiguate multiple assemblies available for the same organism/release pair.

covered_releases()[source]

Return the Ensembl releases that the organism’s externals YAML lists (any form, database or assembly).

Returns:

Releases with at least one entry; empty if the file has no entry for the organism.

Return type:

set[int]

If no externals YAML file exists for the organism, ExternalsError is raised (see load_modified_yaml()).

create_template_yaml(table)[source]

Generate a template YAML enumerating external-database options.

This helper scans table—typically the dataframe returned by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content()—and writes a scaffold configuration file to file_name_template_yaml(). The file lists every organism → form → database combination observed in table, grouped by genome assembly and Ensembl release. For each entry the template records whether the database should be included when building an ID-history graph.

Users are expected to edit the generated file—changing Include from false to true where appropriate—and rename it by appending _modified to the filename before the package will load it. A warning to that effect is emitted via logging.Logger.warning().

The resulting YAML resembles the structure below (truncated for brevity):

homo_sapiens:
    gene:
        ArrayExpress:
            Assembly:
                "37":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89
                    Include: false
                "38":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85,86,87,88,89
                    Include: false
        Clone-based (Ensembl):
            Assembly:
                "37":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85
                    Include: false
                "38":
                    Ensembl release: 79,80,81,82,83,84,85
                    Include: false

Editing guidelines

  • Set Include to true for every assembly of the databases you need.

  • Save the edited file with _modified appended to the base name so that downstream routines load the customised version.

Parameters:

table (pandas.DataFrame) – Dataframe containing at least the columns ["organism", "form", "name_db", "assembly", "release"]. It should be produced by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() so that the expected schema is guaranteed.

Notes

It is important to follow the final warning raised by the method. ‘’Please edit the file based on requested external databases and add ‘_modified’ to the file name.’’. The editing should be done by converting Include sections from false to true. It is recommended to make the change for each assembly for a given database.

extend_modified_yaml(content, output_path=None, base_path=None)[source]

Extend the organism’s modified externals YAML to the releases of a database-content table.

This is the way to bring an existing <organism>_externals_modified.yml up to new Ensembl releases without regenerating and re-curating it. content is the output of idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() for the new releases (build the manager with first_release and snapshot_release set to them). For every (form, database, assembly) that content holds:

  • an existing entry gets the new releases added to its Ensembl release list, and keeps its Include flag;

  • a database that the file does not have yet is added with Include: false and reported under "new_databases", so that a person can decide whether to enable it;

  • a known database that appears with a new assembly gets an entry for that assembly. Its Include flag is true only if the database is Include: true on every assembly it already has (the database is then enabled as a whole, as in the shipped files); otherwise it is false. All such entries are reported under "new_assembly_entries", and the ones switched on, which no person has reviewed, are listed again under "switched_on" and in a warning.

The base file is base_path if given, else the local repository’s copy if present, else the shipped default. The result is written to output_path (default: <local_repository>/<organism>_externals_modified.yml), in the layout of the shipped files, atomically (comments of the base file are not kept). When the file read is replaced, its previous version is kept as <file>.bak. Passing a template as both base_path and output_path extends the template the same way (all its flags are false).

Parameters:

  • content (DataFrame) – Frame with at least the columns organism, form, name_db, assembly and release; rows of other organisms are ignored.

  • output_path (str | None) – Where to write the extended file.

  • base_path (str | None) – File to extend instead of the modified YAML that load_modified_yaml() would read.

Returns:

Report with keys "path" (file written), "releases" (releases of content), "extended_entries" (number of existing entries that gained releases), "new_databases" (list of (form, database, assembly)), "new_assembly_entries" (list of (form, database, assembly, include)) and "switched_on" (list of (form, database, assembly) of the new assembly entries added with Include: true).

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Raises:

ValueError – If content lacks a required column or has no row for the organism.

file_name_modified_yaml(location)[source]

Resolve the path to a modified YAML file customised by the user or shipped with the package.

Two locations are known:

  • "configured" - the user-edited file living in ExternalDatabases.local_repository.

  • "default" - the read-only fallback bundled under <package_root>/default_config for quick starts and unit tests.

By funnelling every lookup through this routine, higher-level helpers such as ExternalDatabases.load_modified_yaml() remain agnostic about the underlying directory structure and can focus on validation and parsing instead.

Parameters:

location (str) – Either "configured" or "default" selecting the corresponding search location.

Returns:

Absolute path of the requested YAML file.

Return type:

str

Raises:

InvalidArgumentError – If location is not one of the two values.

file_name_template_yaml()[source]

Return absolute path to the template YAML configuration file.

A helper that deterministically builds the filename used by ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml() when it first scaffolds the external-database configuration for organism. Centralising the logic here keeps every component of idtrack that may need the path (tests, CLI tools, future maintenance scripts) in perfect sync with a single implementation. The method performs no I/O; it merely concatenates ExternalDatabases.local_repository and the conventional filename pattern "<organism>_externals_template.yml" so callers can decide whether to create, read, or overwrite the file.

Returns:

Absolute path of <organism>_externals_template.yml located inside ExternalDatabases.local_repository.

Return type:

str

give_list_for_case(give_type)[source]

Return database names or assembly codes extracted from the external-DB YAML file.

The helper provides a lightweight way for higher-level components (e.g. DatabaseManager) to discover which external resources—or which genome assemblies—are currently eligible according to the user-editable YAML configuration created by ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml(). Instead of forcing the caller to parse the YAML structure manually, the method filters the entries for the manager’s organism, form, Ensembl release and genome assembly and returns the requested slice.

Parameters:

give_type (str) –

Kind of list to return. Accepted values are

  • "db" external-database names (str) whose Include flag is true for the current organism, form, assembly and Ensembl release.

  • "assembly" genome-assembly codes (int) for which the YAML enables at least one external database (Include: true) at the current Ensembl release, restricted to the assemblies whose release window (organism table) holds that release.

Returns:

  • When give_type is "db", a list of database names.

  • When give_type is "assembly", a list of assembly codes.

Return type:

list[str] | list[int]

Raises:

ValueError – If give_type is not "db" nor "assembly" or if an unexpected internal inconsistency is encountered while traversing the YAML structure.

load_modified_yaml()[source]

Load the user-edited or default YAML configuration and verify release compatibility.

This convenience wrapper searches for the configured YAML file first; if it does not exist or lacks read permissions a warning is logged and the default YAML file shipped with the package is tried instead. Failure to locate either file aborts with an ExternalsError that names the file to create and the documented way to create it. After loading, the method delegates to ExternalDatabases.validate_yaml_file_up_to_date() to ensure that the currently requested Ensembl release is represented in the configuration.

Returns:

Parsed YAML content keyed by {organism → form → database → Assembly → {...}}.

Return type:

dict

read_modified_yaml()[source]

Read the modified YAML (local repository first, then the shipped default) without release checks.

The file is parsed and checked against the organism table once per version of the file (load_externals_yaml()).

Returns:

Parsed YAML content keyed by {organism → form → database → Assembly → {...}}; a copy that the caller may change.

Return type:

dict

If neither the configured nor the default YAML file exists, _modified_yaml_path() raises ExternalsError.

selected_names()[source]

Return the database names the YAML enables for the organism anywhere: any form, assembly or release.

Return type:

set[str]

selected_units()[source]

Return the (form, name) pairs the YAML enables for the organism anywhere (a synonym’s by its entry’s name).

Return type:

set[tuple[str, str]]

settings_release()[source]

Return the release of the externals YAML whose settings apply to the manager’s release.

A release that the file lists takes its own settings. A release after the last one the file lists takes the settings of that last release (for the same form and assembly), so that a new Ensembl release is never built without external databases; a graph records which release’s settings each of its releases took. A release before or between listed releases has none.

Returns:

The release whose settings apply, or None.

Return type:

int | None

validate_yaml_file_up_to_date(read_yaml_file)[source]

Assert that the YAML configuration lists the active Ensembl release.

The external-database mapping evolves with each Ensembl release. This helper extracts the set of releases encoded in read_yaml_file—no matter how deeply nested—and verifies that ExternalDatabases.release is present. Triggering an exception here prevents downstream graph-construction logic from silently operating on incomplete or outdated metadata, prompting users to extend the YAML file (extend_modified_yaml()) before proceeding.

A file that exists but has no entry for the organism or form is accepted: the graph is then built without external databases for it.

Parameters:

read_yaml_file (dict) – Dictionary produced by ExternalDatabases.load_modified_yaml() containing the loaded YAML structure.

Raises:

ExternalsReleaseNotCoveredError – If the current Ensembl release is absent from the YAML configuration (a ValueError).

class VerifyOrganism(name)[source]

Resolve a tentative organism identifier to the formal Ensembl species name and its latest supported release.

The class shields end-users from the quirks of the Ensembl REST payload by converting any synonym—common name, scientific name, assembly name or accession, or NCBI taxon ID—into the canonical Ensembl species identifier (e.g. homo_sapiens) and the newest Ensembl release that still hosts that species. Matching is case-insensitive on both sides. A query equal to a formal name (also written with spaces, e.g. "Macaca mulatta") or to a taxon ID is never ambiguous: a taxon ID that Ensembl also gives to strains or breeds resolves to the species-level entry (9823 → sus_scrofa). Any other synonym that several species share raises an error that lists the candidates, unless idtrack declares it as the alias of one organism (idtrack.organisms.ALIASES: "pig", "human", "mouse", "rhesus", "cynomolgus"; Ensembl lists "pig" as the common name of every pig breed).

The species list comes from one call to the Ensembl REST API per process and day (/info/species, see idtrack.build.ensembl_access.rest_get_json() and idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.rest_species_cache_seconds), made only when it is needed: the formal name of an organism configured in idtrack (idtrack.organisms.supported_organisms(), also written with spaces) and its declared aliases resolve without the network; other synonyms, taxon IDs and the latest release need it.

After construction the instance offers two high-level helpers:

>>> # xdoctest: +REQUIRES(--network)
>>> resolver = VerifyOrganism("human")
>>> resolver.get_formal_name()      # 'homo_sapiens'
>>> resolver.get_latest_release()   # 117  (example)

Both helpers are backed by two public dataframes, loaded on first use:

  • name_synonyms_dataframe — maps every synonym returned by the REST service to the chosen formal name and flags synonyms that are ambiguous across species.

  • ensembl_release_dataframe — one row per Ensembl species (indexed by formal_name) holding its latest Ensembl release number.

The names of the assemblies of the organism table (also of earlier assemblies, e.g. "GRCh37") resolve to their organism without the network; they name the organism, not the assembly. A malformed species entry of Ensembl is left out with a warning, unless it is one of idtrack’s organisms (then it is an error).

Initialise the resolver; nothing is fetched until a look-up needs the Ensembl species list.

Parameters:

name (str | int) – Organism identifier supplied by the user—common name ("human"), shorthand ("hsapiens"), taxon ID (9606 or "9606"), assembly name ("Mmul_10"), or Ensembl species name ("homo_sapiens", "Macaca mulatta"). The value is converted to a stripped, lower-case string before processing.

Raises:

  • ArgumentTypeError – If name is neither a string nor an integer.

  • MissingValueError – If name is an empty string.

This internal utility performs a single call to /info/species on the Ensembl REST server, parses the returned JSON, and constructs two pandas dataframes:

The request uses the timeouts and retries of idtrack.build.ensembl_access.rest_get_json(), whose idtrack.EnsemblRestError propagates when Ensembl does not answer (idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.connection_timeout, idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.reading_timeout, idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.rest_attempts). _species_tables() keeps the result for the process.

Resolve the user’s organism query to the canonical Ensembl species name.

Resolution, in this order (all comparisons on normalised, lower-case strings):

  1. the query is a formal name ("homo_sapiens"), also with spaces or hyphens for underscores ("Macaca mulatta"), or an alias that idtrack declares for an organism ("pig"); for an organism configured in idtrack this needs no network;

  2. the query is a taxon ID: the organism with that ID, or—when Ensembl gives the ID to several strains or breeds—the species-level entry (the formal name of two words, sus_scrofa for 9823);

  3. any other synonym of name_synonyms_dataframe (common names, display names, assembly names and accessions, aliases), which must belong to exactly one organism.

str

Raises:

This helper calls get_formal_name() to resolve the user-supplied organism query to the canonical Ensembl species name, then looks up that key in the dataframe prepared at instantiation time. Down-stream routines (e.g. database connectors, file download helpers) rely on this value to decide which Ensembl release to fetch, ensuring the entire pipeline stays on a single, internally consistent genome build.

Loading the result with yaml.safe_load() gives back data.

Allowlists of the externals YAML files shipped in idtrack/default_config.

A shipped <organism>_externals_modified.yml is the organism’s template (made by idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_database_content() and idtrack.ExternalDatabases.create_template_yaml() over every release and form) with Include: true set for the (form, database, assembly) entries of the organism’s allowlist below, by apply_allowlist(). Nothing else differs between template and modified file. The lists follow one conceptual set for every organism, with the species’ own symbol databases:

  • gene: clone-based, Havana and Vega names, RFAM with its labels (RFAM label, the names of the genes whose display name they are), miRBase with its labels (miRBase label, on miRNA genes only), UniProtKB gene names, the species’ symbol source(s), and the synonym_id:: forms of the identifier and symbol databases;

  • transcript: CCDS with its labels (CCDS label, the versioned accessions), Havana transcripts and RefSeq mRNA / ncRNA (curated and predicted);

  • translation: Havana translations, RefSeq peptides (curated and predicted) and UniProt (Swiss-Prot, TrEMBL);

  • every form: NCBI’s gene ids (EntrezGene) with their labels (NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)) and synonyms (NCBI_GENE).

A list names a database by what it is; the graph reads it on every form and at every release at which Ensembl has it (NCBI’s gene ids on translations up to release 62 and on genes from 63, Rfam’s and miRBase’s accessions on transcripts up to 62, MGI’s symbols on translations up to 51), and with it every database of Ensembl whose links continue it (RefSeq’s mRNA accessions under RefSeq_dna up to release 63, the HGNC projections of pig and macaque genes under HGNC_curated_gene and HGNC_automatic_gene up to 60): decision 104, idtrack.DatabaseManager.database_filing(). The species’ symbol source is what Ensembl names the genes by today. The names Ensembl gave the genes at a release, under whatever database it filed them (UniProt’s entry names, clone-based names), are in the graph whatever this list says: a gene’s display name at a release is a name of the gene at that release (idtrack.DatabaseManager.create_external_db()).

Names that an organism’s template does not contain are skipped. Tutorial 02 (docs/_notebooks/02_prepare_new_external_yaml.ipynb) shows the same lists as editable dictionaries.

NCBI_GENE: tuple[str, ...] = ('EntrezGene', 'NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)', 'synonym_id::NCBI gene (formerly Entrezgene)')

listed on every form, since Ensembl attached them to translations up to release 62 and to genes from 63 (the graph reads a selected database on every form in any case).

Type:

NCBI’s gene ids, their labels and their synonyms

Storage of idtrack’s cached tables: one immutable HDF5 file per table, written atomically.

Every table that idtrack.DatabaseManager downloads or computes is kept in a file of its own (<directory>/<table key>.h5). A table is written completely to a private temporary file in the same directory, flushed to disk and only then renamed to its final name (os.replace(), atomic on POSIX file systems), so:

  • a table that is visible is complete: a process killed in the middle of a write (time limit, out of memory, closed kernel) leaves the repository as it was, apart from an orphaned temporary file that no reader ever opens;

  • finished files are never opened for writing again, so readers need no lock and are never blocked by writers, and two processes that compute the same table at the same time both succeed (the last rename wins, with a complete table);

  • replacing a table frees the space of the old one (there is no in-file deletion that HDF5 cannot reclaim).

Each file records the storage format version and the parameters the table was computed with (write_table()); load_table() returns a table only if both match what the caller asks for, so a table made under other parameters is never served.

The format stores every column by position (labels and dtypes are metadata), text as dictionary codes plus the distinct values as one compressed UTF-8 byte buffer with offsets (missing values are code -1, never a sentinel string), categoricals as codes plus categories, datetimes and timedeltas as int64 with their exact unit, and numbers and booleans as they are, all chunked with the shuffle filter and gzip level 4. A table read back equals the table written (DataFrame.equals and identical dtypes; text comes back in the default text dtype of the running pandas, object under pandas 2 and str under pandas 3, with NaN for missing values, which is what pandas produces for freshly computed text). Files are written with the HDF5 format bounds ("earliest", "v110"), so a file written with any HDF5 library from 1.10 on is readable by every other.

TABLE_FORMAT_VERSION = 2

Version of the on-disk table format; a file of another version is not read (the table is recomputed).

load_table(path, params, logger=None)[source]

Return the table stored at path if it was computed with exactly params, else None.

None means “compute the table”: the file is absent, of another format version, made with other parameters, or unreadable (a damaged file is reported once in the log and then replaced by the caller’s next write).

Parameters:

  • path (str) – The table file.

  • params (dict[str, Any]) – The parameters the caller needs (compared with those recorded by write_table()).

  • logger (Logger | None) – Where to report a damaged or mismatching file; the module logger by default.

Returns:

The table, or None.

Return type:

Optional[pandas.DataFrame]

read_table(path)[source]

Read a table written by write_table().

Parameters:

path (str) – The table file.

Returns:

The table as written (see the module docstring for text dtypes).

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If path does not exist.

Notes

How idtrack reaches Ensembl: the access mode and the per-process reachability of TCP ports.

Ensembl serves the same core databases two ways: the public MySQL service (ensembldb.ensembl.org, ports 3306, 5306 and 3337) and the MySQL dumps on https://ftp.ensembl.org/pub/. Many networks block the MySQL ports, and a blocked port costs a full connect timeout every time it is tried. This module makes that cost a one-off:

  • ensembl_access_mode() returns the access mode, "auto" (MySQL where its port answers, the HTTPS dumps otherwise) or "https" (MySQL is never touched), from idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.access or the IDTRACK_ENSEMBL_ACCESS environment variable.

  • reachability (a PortReachability) probes a (host, port) once per process with a short timeout and remembers the answer. Every code path that would open a MySQL connection asks it first, and a connection that fails after a successful probe marks the port unreachable for the rest of the process.

  • rest_get_json() is the one way idtrack asks Ensembl REST, and https_get() the one way it reads the HTTPS dumps: both with the timeouts of idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.connection_timeout and idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.reading_timeout, the same retries, and an error that says what failed and what to change (idtrack.EnsemblRestError, EnsemblDownloadError). https_get() tells “absent” (HTTP 404 or 410 from a server that answered) apart from “unknown” (time-out, connection error, 429, 5xx), which is retried and, if it stays unknown, raised: a failed request is never read as “does not exist”.

The results do not depend on the mode: both paths read the same Ensembl tables, with the same column types.

class PortReachability[source]

Remember, per process, whether a TCP (host, port) accepts connections.

The first question about a (host, port) opens one TCP connection with a short timeout (idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.mysql_probe_timeout unless given); later questions are answered from memory. mark_unreachable() records a failure observed elsewhere: a MySQL connection that fails after a successful probe (refused, dropped or lost during a query) marks the port unreachable. A “reachable” answer is kept for the life of the process; an “unreachable” one expires, so that a long-running process does not stay on the slower HTTPS dumps for days after one network blip: after retry_after_seconds (10 minutes) the port is probed again, and every further failure doubles the wait, up to max_retry_after_seconds (one day). The memory is process-wide, so parallel requests do not each wait for a probe. Unreachable ports only cost speed: the tables are then read from the HTTPS dumps, which hold the same rows.

Create an empty reachability memory.

can_connect(host, port, timeout_s=None)[source]

Return whether (host, port) accepts TCP connections, probing it only the first time.

Parameters:

  • host (str) – Host name.

  • port (int) – TCP port.

  • timeout_s (float | None) – Connect timeout of the probe in seconds; defaults to idtrack.settings.ENSEMBL.mysql_probe_timeout.

Returns:

The remembered (or freshly probed) answer.

Return type:

bool

mark_unreachable(host, port, reason=None)[source]

Record that (host, port) failed, so that it is not tried again for a while (see the class docstring).

A transient failure therefore sends later tables to the HTTPS dumps for that while, which costs speed but not correctness.

Parameters:

  • port (int) – TCP port.

  • reason (str | None) – Optional text for the log message.

None

HTTP 404 and 410 mean the file does not exist. The connection is reused within a thread.

Any other HTTP status is not retried.

Read Ensembl’s MySQL table dumps (<table>.txt.gz) exactly as MySQL would load them.

The dumps are written by SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE with the default FIELDS TERMINATED BY '\t' ESCAPED BY '\\' LINES TERMINATED BY '\n'. In that format a backslash escapes the next character: a field that holds a tab or a newline is written as a backslash followed by the raw tab or newline, a backslash as \\, NUL as \0, and SQL NULL as a field consisting of \N. LOAD DATA also reads \b, \n, \r, \t and \Z as backspace, newline, carriage return, tab and Ctrl-Z. Any other escaped character stands for itself. Raw carriage returns are ordinary data (only \n ends a record).

Reading such a file with a plain tab-separated parser splits a record at every escaped newline, keeps the escaping backslashes and treats a leading double quote as CSV quoting. read_mysql_dump() instead decodes each record the way LOAD DATA does and hands pandas an unambiguous CSV stream, so the frame matches what the MySQL server returns for the same table (NULL becomes NaN; pandas infers the column dtypes as it does for any text input). Records without escapes or quotes, the vast majority, pass through untouched.

class MySQLDumpCSVStream(source, chunk_size=1048576)[source]

Text stream that turns a MySQL dump into CSV that pandas parses unambiguously.

Records are read from source (a text stream of the dump) and written out as tab-separated CSV records: records without backslash escapes or double quotes are passed through; the others are decoded field by field, and fields containing a tab, newline or double quote are quoted. SQL NULL stays \N (read by pandas as NaN through na_values). Values that pandas cannot reproduce verbatim are emitted as empty fields and recorded in restore as (record index, field index, value) for read_mysql_dump() to put back.

Parameters:

  • source (Any) – Readable text stream of the dump (already decompressed).

  • chunk_size (int) – Number of characters read from source at a time.

Wrap source; nothing is read until read() is called.

read(size=-1)[source]

Return up to size characters of CSV (everything that is left when size is negative or None).

Parameters:

size (int | None)

Return type:

str

Return True: the stream supports read().

Return type:

bool

  • usecols (list[str] | None) – Optional subset of columns to keep (in this order).

  • text_columns (Collection[str]) – Columns that the schema declares as text (character, enumeration, date and time types); they are read as text in the default text dtype of pandas, so their type does not depend on their content.

Returns:

One row per record; SQL NULL is NaN; empty strings stay empty strings.

Return type:

pandas.DataFrame

Resolve an organism’s name through Ensembl REST (common names, taxon ids, assembly names) to its Ensembl name.

The path of Ensembl REST’s species list, below idtrack.settings.EnsemblSettings.rest_server.

The manager of an organism’s Ensembl tables: download (MySQL or HTTPS), store, derive what a graph needs.

ASSEMBLY_EXCEPTION_COLUMNS = ['seq_region_id', 'seq_region_start', 'seq_region_end', 'exc_type', 'exc_seq_region_id', 'exc_seq_region_start', 'exc_seq_region_end']

The columns of Ensembl’s assembly_exception table that idtrack reads (DatabaseManager.create_assembly_exceptions()).

BIOTYPE_RESTRICTED: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {'miRBase': frozenset({'miRNA'})}

a miRBase name is the name of the miRNA gene, not of the protein-coding gene that hosts it.

Type:

Databases whose identifiers are kept only on genes of the given biotypes

CHROMOSOME_COORD_SYSTEM = 'chromosome'

the coordinate system of the chromosomes (coord_system.name), the attribute by which Ensembl ranks a region in the organism’s karyotype (the chromosomes of an assembly loaded with one level of sequences, whose coordinate system is primary_assembly), and the attribute of a region translated with an alternate genetic code (in a vertebrate core database, the mitochondrial genome alone).

Type:

Ensembl’s names that say what a sequence region is (idtrack.graph.types.Place.kind)

DERIVED_GENE_NAME_SUFFIX = '_gene_name'

Ensembl files the names it derives from an external database for genes under a database of their own, named after it: <db_name>_gene_name (miRBase_gene_name: the names of miRBase that Ensembl displays on genes at releases 61 and 62, RFAM_gene_name). Such a name is a name of the database it is derived from, and that database’s definitions (BIOTYPE_RESTRICTED, ONE_GENE_ONLY) hold for it whatever name it is filed under (rules_database()). Ensembl’s names of transcripts (<db_name>_trans_name: the gene’s name and a number, FZD5-201) are Ensembl’s own names, not names of that database.

DISPLAY_LABEL_ONLY: frozenset[str] = frozenset({'RFAM'})

the label of a family (5S_rRNA, U6, SNORD115) is Ensembl’s name of the genes that have no better name, not a name of every member of the family. They are the databases of families (idtrack.settings.FAMILY_DATABASES), whose accessions are no bridge between genes either.

Type:

Databases whose labels name a gene only where the label is the gene’s display name (gene.display_xref_id)

EXTERNAL_RULES_VERSION = 10

Version of the rules that derive the tables of cross references from Ensembl’s raw tables; a stored table derived under other rules is derived again.

GENE_ANNOTATION_COLUMNS = ['gene_id', 'biotype', 'display_xref_id', 'seq_region_id', 'seq_region_start', 'seq_region_end', 'seq_region_strand']

Columns of the gene table that say what a gene is and where it lies.

NON_REFERENCE_ATTRIBUTE = 'non_ref'

The code of the attribute by which Ensembl’s core databases mark a sequence region that is not part of the reference sequence of an assembly (attrib_type.code: an alternative locus, an assembly patch or an LRG record).

ONE_GENE_ONLY: frozenset[str] = frozenset({'miRBase'})

Databases whose entries link a gene only where Ensembl gives the entry to one gene over all the releases of a graph: a miRBase entry that Ensembl attaches to genes at several loci, at once (copies of one precursor at several loci) or one after the other (an accession moved to a gene at another locus), is no evidence of which gene it is; as a link it ties those genes, and carries retired ids and old names to the others. An entry is left out only where the graph shows two loci, by the package’s one rule (idtrack.graph.genes.count_genes()): two genes that live at one release at places that do not overlap (a split of one id into two that live side by side is two genes), or genes one after the other at places apart on one assembly or on chromosomes of different names; ids that Ensembl’s history carried one to the other where they follow one another, or whose places overlap, are one gene, a copy outside the reference sequence adds none, and holders on two assemblies that nothing compares (no history link, no comparable place) are no evidence of two loci (idtrack.build.GraphMaker.construct_graph()). A link on a transcript or a translation counts for the gene that holds it at the releases of the link.

XREF_COLUMNS = ['xref_id', 'external_db_id', 'dbprimary_acc', 'display_label', 'version']

the entry, its database, its accession and label, and the version of the accession that the cross reference attaches (xref.version; 0 where the database gives none).

Type:

The columns of Ensembl’s xref table that idtrack reads

label_name(database, names=None)[source]

Return the name of a database’s label rows: its name in names, else <database> label.

  • database (str) – The database’s db_name.

  • names (Mapping[str, str] | None) – The names of the label rows of a window (label_names_of_databases()); a database that no external_db of the window has is not in it.

Returns:

The name of the database’s label rows.

Return type:

str

label_names_of_databases(rows)[source]

Return the one name that every database’s label rows take at every release of a window.

One database name means one kind of identifier at every release. Ensembl names a database’s label rows by its display name (external_db.db_display_name), which changes over the releases for some databases and is, at some releases, also the name of a database’s accessions (a db_name of the release: the labels and the accessions of EntrezGene share that name up to release 87, RFAM’s always). The labels of a database are named, at every release, by its display name at the newest release of the window at which that display name is not the name of accessions; a database whose display name always is takes <db_name> label.

Parameters:

rows (Iterable[tuple[int, str, str | None, frozenset[str]]]) – (release, db_name, db_display_name, the db_name of every database of that release) for every database of every release (and assembly) of the window.

Returns:

{db_name: name of its label rows}.

Return type:

dict[str, str]
